translations.idiomatic: "In the East There Is a Worthy Woman."

translations.literal: "In the Second Year of Zhanghe."
translations.idiomatic: "In the Second Year of Zhanghe."

translations.literal: "May Joy Endure Long."
translations.idiomatic: "May Joy Endure Long."

translations.literal: "Sovereign of the Four Quarters."
translations.idiomatic: "Sovereign of the Four Quarters."

translations.idiomatic: "Before the Hall Grows an Osmanthus Tree."

translations.literal: Wei "Piwu Dance Songs," five pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Five Wei dynasty Battle-Drum Dance songs.

translations.literal: "Bright and Illustrious Is the Emperor of Wei."
translations.idiomatic: "Bright and Illustrious Is the Emperor of Wei."

translations.literal: "In the Taihe Era There Was a Sage Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: "In the Taihe Era There Was a Sage Emperor."

translations.literal: "Long Last the Wei Calendar."
translations.idiomatic: "Long Last the Wei Calendar."

translations.literal: "Heaven Born the Multitudes."

translations.idiomatic: "To Be a Ruler Is Already No Easy Matter."

translations.literal: Wei Prince Si of Chen "Piwu Dance Songs," five pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Five Battle-Drum Dance songs by Prince Si of Chen of Wei (Cao Zhi).

translations.literal: "The Sage Emperor" — to the tune of "In the Second Year of Zhanghe."
translations.idiomatic: "The Sage Emperor" — to be sung to the tune of "In the Second Year of Zhanghe."

sentences.zh: 聖皇應歷數，正康帝道休。

translations.literal: The sage emperor responds to the cycles of fate; now upright is the imperial Way, and repose prevails.
translations.idiomatic: The sage emperor answers to Heaven's mandate; the royal Way stands firm and the realm is at peace.

sentences.zh: 九州咸賓服，威德洞八幽。

translations.literal: The nine provinces all come as guests in submission; majesty and virtue penetrate the eight hidden realms.
translations.idiomatic: All the nine provinces bow in allegiance; his majesty and virtue reach to the furthest corners of creation.

sentences.zh: 三公奏諸公，不得久淹留。

translations.literal: The Three Dukes present their memorials on the nobles; they may not linger long in delay.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dukes report on the imperial princes—they cannot be kept waiting at court.

sentences.zh: 蕃位任至重，舊章咸率由。

translations.literal: The feudatory posts bear utmost weight; ancient statutes all are led and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Their princely appointments carry the gravest responsibility; every one must follow the laws of old.

sentences.zh: 侍臣省文奏，陛下體仁慈。

translations.literal: Attendant ministers review documents and memorialize; Your Majesty embodies benevolence and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers lay the papers before him, yet the Emperor's heart is mercy itself.

sentences.zh: 沈吟有愛戀，不忍聽可之。

translations.literal: He ponders deeply, cherishing affection; he cannot bear to hear and assent to it.
translations.idiomatic: He hesitates, bound by love, unwilling even to hear the proposal granted.

sentences.zh: 迫有官典憲，不得顧恩私。

translations.literal: Constrained by the officials' codes and statutes, he cannot turn to private favor.
translations.idiomatic: But royal law and ordinance compel him—private feeling may not prevail.

sentences.zh: 諸王當就國，璽綬何纍縗。

translations.literal: The princes ought to go to their states; how heavily hang seal and ribbon?
translations.idiomatic: The princes must depart for their domains—how weighty are the seal and sash upon them!

sentences.zh: 便時舍外殿，宮省寂無人。

translations.literal: At the appointed time they leave the outer halls; palace departments stand empty without a soul.
translations.idiomatic: At the hour appointed they quit the outer palace; the halls fall silent and bare.

sentences.zh: 主上增顧念，皇母懷苦辛。

translations.literal: The sovereign redoubles his solicitude; the empress dowager harbors bitter grief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's thoughts turn to them ever more; the Empress Dowager grieves in her heart.

sentences.zh: 何以為贈賜，傾府竭寶珍。

translations.literal: What shall serve as gifts and bestowals? The treasury is emptied of precious treasures.
translations.idiomatic: What gifts shall he send? He drains the treasury of its treasures.

sentences.zh: 文錢百億萬，采帛若煙雲。

translations.literal: Coin in writing a hundred million myriad; colored silks like mist and clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Copper cash by the billion, brocades and silks piled like clouds.

sentences.zh: 乘輿服御物，錦羅與金銀。

translations.literal: Carriage and apparel and furnishings for imperial use—brocade, gauze, and gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Chariots, robes, and regalia of state—brocades, gauzes, gold, and silver.

sentences.zh: 龍旗垂九旒，羽蓋參班輪。

translations.literal: The dragon banner trails nine tassels; feathered canopy sets its ranks with wheel-spokes.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon banners hang with nine tasselled pennants; feathered canopies wheel with the carriage.

sentences.zh: 諸王自計念，無功荷厚德。

translations.literal: The princes reflect on themselves: no merit, yet bearing heavy favor.
translations.idiomatic: Each prince reflects: he has no merit to show, yet bears such overwhelming grace.

sentences.zh: 思一效筋力，糜軀以報國。

translations.literal: He longs to exert his sinews once: to spend his body in repaying the state.
translations.idiomatic: He yearns to give all his strength, to spend himself in service to the realm.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚{扌雝}節衛，副使隨經營。

translations.literal: The Grand Herald arranges ceremonial guards; deputy envoys follow in managing the journey.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Herald marshals the escort; deputy commissioners attend to every detail.

sentences.zh: 貴戚竝出送，夾道交輜軿。

translations.literal: Nobles and kin all come out to escort; along the road carriages meet wheel to wheel.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen of the imperial clan turn out to see them off; the road is choked with carriages.

sentences.zh: 車服齊整設，韡曅燿天精。

translations.literal: Carriages and robes arrayed in order; splendor blazing like heaven's essence.
translations.idiomatic: Chariots and vestments stand in perfect array, blazing bright as heaven's light.

sentences.zh: 武騎衛前後，鼓吹簫笳聲。

translations.literal: Armed horsemen guard fore and aft; drums and pipes, flute and reed pipe sound.
translations.idiomatic: Armed horsemen ride before and behind; drums and pipes, flutes and reeds resound.

sentences.zh: 祖道魏東門，淚下霑冠纓。

translations.literal: Farewell rites at Wei's eastern gate; tears soak the cap-strings.
translations.idiomatic: At the eastern gate of Wei the farewell rites are held; tears soak the cap-strings.

sentences.zh: 扳蓋因內顧，俛仰慕同生。

translations.literal: Lifting the canopy, he looks back within; bowing low, yearning toward those born of the same womb.
translations.idiomatic: He lifts the carriage hood and looks back within; bowing low, he yearns toward those born of one womb.

sentences.zh: 行行將日莫，何時還闕庭。

translations.literal: Step by step the day will set; when shall he return to the palace court?
translations.idiomatic: Step by step the sun sinks low—when shall he return to the palace court?

sentences.zh: 車輪為裴回，四馬躊躇鳴。

translations.literal: The carriage wheels turn back; four horses hesitate and neigh.
translations.idiomatic: The wheels turn back upon themselves; the four horses linger and neigh.

sentences.zh: 路人尚酸鼻，何況骨肉情。

translations.literal: Passersby still smart in the nose—how much more those of flesh and bone!
translations.idiomatic: Even strangers are moved to tears—how much more those bound by flesh and blood!

translations.literal: "The Lingzhi" — to the tune of "Before the Hall Grows an Osmanthus Tree."
translations.idiomatic: "The Lingzhi" — to be sung to the tune of "Before the Hall Grows an Osmanthus Tree."

sentences.zh: 靈芝生玉地，朱草被洛濱。

translations.literal: Lingzhi grows on jade ground; cinnabar grass covers the Luo's banks.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhi mushrooms spring from jade-like soil; crimson grass carpets the banks of the Luo.

sentences.zh: 榮華相晃燿，光采曄若神。

translations.literal: Glory and splendor flash upon each other; radiance gleams as if divine.
translations.idiomatic: Their glory flashes one upon another; their radiance gleams like the divine.

sentences.zh: 古時有虞舜，父母頑且嚚。

translations.literal: In antiquity there was Yu Shun; his parents were stubborn and perverse.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times there was Yu Shun, whose parents were stubborn and harsh.

sentences.zh: 盡孝於田隴，烝烝不違仁。

translations.literal: He fulfilled filial piety in the fields and ridges; ever earnest, he never strayed from humaneness.
translations.idiomatic: He practiced filial piety in the fields, ever earnest, never straying from the humane Way.

sentences.zh: 伯瑜年七十，采衣以娛親。

translations.literal: Bo Yu at age seventy wore colored garments to delight his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Lao Laizi at seventy still donned bright clothes to amuse his parents.

sentences.zh: 慈母笞不痛，歔欷涕沾巾。

translations.literal: When his loving mother beat him he felt no pain; he sobbed and wept, soaking his kerchief.
translations.idiomatic: When his loving mother struck him he felt no pain; he sobbed until his kerchief was soaked with tears.

sentences.zh: 丁蘭少失母，自傷蚤孤煢，

translations.literal: Ding Lan in youth lost his mother; he grieved that he was orphaned early and alone,
translations.idiomatic: Ding Lan lost his mother in youth and mourned that he had been orphaned so young,

sentences.zh: 刻木當嚴親，朝夕致三牲。

translations.literal: he carved wood to stand for his stern parent, morning and evening offering the three sacrificial beasts.
translations.idiomatic: so he carved wood to represent his departed parent and offered the three sacrificial beasts morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 暴子見陵侮，犯辠以亡形，

translations.literal: Bao Zi suffered insult and abuse; for his offense his form was lost,
translations.idiomatic: When Bao Zi was abused and insulted, he committed a crime and lost his life,

sentences.zh: 丈人為泣血，免戾全其名。

translations.literal: his father-in-law wept blood for him; guilt was remitted and his name preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: yet his father-in-law wept blood for him until his guilt was pardoned and his good name preserved.

sentences.zh: 董永遭家貧，父老財無遺。

translations.literal: Dong Yong met with household poverty; when his father grew old, no wealth remained.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yong's family was poor; when his father grew old, nothing was left of their wealth.

sentences.zh: 舉假以供養，傭作致甘肥。

translations.literal: He borrowed to supply their support; hired labor brought sweet and rich fare.
translations.idiomatic: He borrowed money to support him and hired himself out to provide fine food.

sentences.zh: 責家填門至，不知何用歸。

translations.literal: Creditors filled the door arriving; he knew not what use to make of returning.
translations.idiomatic: When creditors crowded his door, he did not know how he could ever repay them.

sentences.zh: 天靈感至德，神女為秉機。

translations.literal: Heaven's spirit responded to utmost virtue; a divine woman took up the loom for him.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven was moved by his supreme virtue, and a goddess came to weave for him.

sentences.zh: 歲月不安居，烏乎我皇考！

translations.literal: Years and months—no settled dwelling; alas, my august father!
translations.idiomatic: The years bring no peace—alas, my revered father!

sentences.zh: 生我既已晚，棄我何期蚤！

translations.literal: He bore me already late; why did he forsake me so soon!
translations.idiomatic: You bore me late in life—why did you leave me so soon!

translations.literal: "The Lad's Wort"—who first raised it? To think on it makes one grow old.
translations.idiomatic: Who first composed "The Lad's Wort"? To dwell on it is to grow old before one's time.

sentences.zh: 退詠《南風》詩，灑淚滿褘抱。

translations.literal: He withdraws to chant the "Southern Breeze" ode; tears cascade, filling his robe's embrace.
translations.idiomatic: He turns to recite the "Southern Breeze" and weeps until his robes are drenched.

translations.literal: Envoi:
translations.idiomatic: Envoi:

sentences.zh: 聖皇君四海，德教朝夕宣。

translations.literal: The sage emperor rules the four seas; virtue and teaching are proclaimed morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: The sage emperor rules the four seas; his virtue and teaching are proclaimed dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 萬國咸禮讓，百姓家肅虔。

translations.literal: Ten thousand states all practice courtesy and yielding; common folk in every home are reverent.
translations.idiomatic: Every land practices courtesy and deference; in every household the people are reverent.

sentences.zh: 庠序不失儀，孝悌處中田。

translations.literal: Schools do not lose their rites; filial piety and brotherly duty dwell in the central fields.
translations.idiomatic: The schools never neglect their rites; filial sons and dutiful brothers fill the countryside.

sentences.zh: 戶有曾閔子，比屋皆仁賢。

translations.literal: Every household has its Zeng Shen or Min Ziqian; house by house, all are humane and worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Every household has its paragon of filial piety; under every roof live the humane and worthy.

sentences.zh: 髫齓無夭齒，黃發盡其年。

translations.literal: Children in their hair-knots know no early death; white-haired elders fulfill their years.
translations.idiomatic: No child dies before his time; the white-haired live out their full span.

sentences.zh: 陛下三萬歲，慈母亦復然。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty live thirty thousand years; may the loving mother likewise!
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty live ten thousand years—and may the Empress Dowager do the same!

translations.literal: "Great Wei" — to the tune of "Han Auspicious and Flourishing."
translations.idiomatic: "Great Wei" — to be sung to the tune of "Han Auspicious and Flourishing."

sentences.zh: 大魏應靈符，天祿方甫始。

translations.literal: Great Wei responds to the numinous tally; Heaven's blessing has just begun.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wei answers to the divine mandate; Heaven's blessing has only just begun.

sentences.zh: 聖德致泰和，神明為驅使。

translations.literal: Sage virtue brings supreme harmony; spirits and gods serve as its drivers.
translations.idiomatic: His sage virtue brings supreme harmony; spirits and gods do his bidding.

sentences.zh: 左右宜供養，中殿宜皇子。

translations.literal: Those at left and right ought to attend his nurture; the central hall ought to hold imperial sons.
translations.idiomatic: Let those at his side attend him well; let the central hall be filled with imperial sons.

sentences.zh: 陛下長壽考，羣臣拜賀咸說喜。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty enjoy long life and vigor; the host of ministers bow in congratulation, all rejoicing.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty enjoy long life; the ministers bow in congratulation, all rejoicing.

sentences.zh: 積善有餘慶，榮祿固天常。

translations.literal: Accumulated goodness has surplus blessing; glory and emolument are firmly Heaven's constant.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulated goodness brings overflowing blessing; rank and reward are Heaven's constant law.

sentences.zh: 眾善填門至，臣子蒙福祥。

translations.literal: Every goodness fills the door arriving; ministers and sons receive fortune and auspice.
translations.idiomatic: Every blessing crowds the threshold; ministers and subjects receive fortune and grace.

sentences.zh: 無患及陽遂，輔翼我聖皇。

translations.literal: No affliction reaches the sun's culmination; assist and wing our sage emperor.
translations.idiomatic: No harm shall touch him to his journey's end; support and sustain our sage emperor.

sentences.zh: 眾吉咸集會，凶邪姦惡竝滅亡。

translations.literal: All auspice gathers together; the inauspicious, perverse, treacherous, and wicked perish together.
translations.idiomatic: All good fortune gathers round; the evil, the perverse, and the wicked perish together.

sentences.zh: 黃鵠游殿前，神鼎週四阿。

translations.literal: Yellow swans roam before the halls; the sacred cauldron circles the four corners.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow swans glide before the palace halls; the sacred tripod stands at every corner.

sentences.zh: 玉馬充乘輿，芝蓋樹九華。

translations.literal: Jade horses fill the imperial carriage; lingzhi canopies raise nine splendors.
translations.idiomatic: Jade horses fill the imperial carriage; lingzhi canopies bloom with ninefold glory.

sentences.zh: 白虎戲西除，舍利從辟邪。

translations.literal: White tigers sport in the western cloister; Buddhist relics follow to ward off evil.
translations.idiomatic: White tigers sport in the western cloister; sacred relics ward off evil spirits.

sentences.zh: 騏驎躡足舞，鳳凰拊翼歌。

translations.literal: Qilin tread and dance; phoenixes beat their wings and sing.
translations.idiomatic: Qilin tread in dance; phoenixes beat their wings and sing.

sentences.zh: 豐年大置酒，玉尊列廣庭。

translations.literal: In a bountiful year, great wine is set out; jade goblets line the broad courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: In this bountiful year great banquets are spread; jade goblets line the broad courtyard.

sentences.zh: 樂飲過三爵，朱顏暴已形。

translations.literal: Joyful drinking passes three rounds; flushed faces already show their form.
translations.idiomatic: They drink past the third round; flushed faces already show their joy.

sentences.zh: 式宴不違禮，君臣歌《鹿鳴》。

translations.literal: The feast proceeds without violating ritual; lord and ministers sing "The Cry of the Deer."
translations.idiomatic: The feast observes every rite; lord and ministers sing "The Cry of the Deer."

sentences.zh: 樂人舞鼙鼓，百官靁抃贊若驚。

translations.literal: Musicians dance to battle drums; the hundred officials thunder-clap in praise as if startled.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians dance to battle drums; the hundred officials clap and shout praise like thunder.

sentences.zh: 儲禮如江海，積善若陵山。

translations.literal: Stored ritual is like rivers and seas; accumulated goodness like mound and mountain.
translations.idiomatic: His stored ritual is deep as rivers and seas; his accumulated goodness high as hills and mountains.

sentences.zh: 皇嗣繁且熾，孫子列曾玄。

translations.literal: Imperial heirs are numerous and flourishing; grandsons and sons line up through great-great-grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial heirs multiply and flourish; sons and grandsons stretch through generations.

sentences.zh: 羣臣咸稱萬歲，陛下長樂壽年！

translations.literal: The host of ministers all cry "Ten thousand years!" May Your Majesty long enjoy joy and years of life!
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all cry "Ten thousand years!" May Your Majesty long enjoy joy and long life!

sentences.zh: 御酒停未飲，貴戚跪東廂。

translations.literal: Imperial wine pauses, not yet drunk; noble kin kneel in the eastern wing.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial wine stands untouched; noble kinsmen kneel in the eastern wing.

sentences.zh: 侍人承顏色，奉進金玉觴。

translations.literal: Attendants read his expression and bearing, presenting the gold and jade goblet.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants read his expression and present the gold and jade goblet.

sentences.zh: 此酒亦真酒，福祿當聖皇。

translations.literal: This wine too is true wine; fortune and emolument belong to the sage emperor.
translations.idiomatic: This too is true wine; fortune and blessing belong to the sage emperor.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨軒笑，左右咸歡康。

translations.literal: Your Majesty faces the hall and smiles; those at left and right are all joyous and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty faces the hall and smiles; all around him rejoice in peace.

sentences.zh: 桮來一何遲，羣僚以次行。

translations.literal: How slow the cup's coming! The host of officials proceed in turn.
translations.idiomatic: How slow the cup arrives! The officials advance in their proper order.

sentences.zh: 賞賜累千億，百官竝富昌。

translations.literal: Rewards and gifts accumulate in thousands of millions; the hundred officials together grow rich and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards pile up by the billion; every official grows rich and prosperous.

translations.literal: "Subtle Essence" — to the tune of "In the East There Is a Worthy Woman."
translations.idiomatic: "Subtle Essence" — to be sung to the tune of "In the East There Is a Worthy Woman."

sentences.zh: 精微爛金石，至心動神明。

translations.literal: Subtle essence blazes through metal and stone; utmost sincerity moves spirits and gods.
translations.idiomatic: Subtle sincerity pierces metal and stone; utmost devotion moves spirits and gods.

sentences.zh: 杞妻哭死夫，梁山為之傾。

translations.literal: Qi Ji's wife wept for her dead husband; Mount Liang tilted for her sake.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Ji's wife mourned her dead husband, Mount Liang tilted for her grief.

sentences.zh: 子丹西質秦，烏白馬角生。

translations.literal: Danzi went west as hostage to Qin; the crow turned white and the horse grew horns.
translations.idiomatic: When Danzi went west as hostage to Qin, crows turned white and horses sprouted horns.

sentences.zh: 鄒羨囚燕市，繁霜為夏零。

translations.literal: Zou Xian was imprisoned in Yan's market; heavy frost fell as summer's frost.
translations.idiomatic: When Zou Xian was imprisoned in Yan's market, heavy frost fell in midsummer.

sentences.zh: 關東有賢女，自字蘇來卿。

translations.literal: In the east there is a worthy woman; she styles herself Su Laiqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the east there was a worthy woman who styled herself Su Laiqing.

sentences.zh: 壯年報父仇，身沒垂功名。

translations.literal: In her prime she avenged her father's death; though her body perished, her fame endures.
translations.idiomatic: In her prime she avenged her father; though she died, her fame endures.

sentences.zh: 女休逢赦書，白刃幾在頸。

translations.literal: Nü Xiu met the amnesty edict; the bright blade was nearly at her neck.
translations.idiomatic: Nü Xiu received the amnesty edict when the bright blade was nearly at her neck.

sentences.zh: 俱上列僊籍，去死獨就生。

translations.literal: Both ascended to the roster of immortals; leaving death, alone they attained life.
translations.idiomatic: Both were entered on the register of immortals; they left death behind and attained life alone.

sentences.zh: 太倉令有辠，遠徵當就拘。

translations.literal: The Grand Granary Director had a crime; summoned from afar, he was to be taken into custody.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Grand Granary had committed a crime and was summoned from afar to be taken into custody.

sentences.zh: 自悲居無男，禍至無與俱。

translations.literal: He grieved that his household had no son; when calamity came, none could share it with him.
translations.idiomatic: He grieved that his home had no son—when disaster struck, no one could share his burden.

sentences.zh: 緹縈痛父言，何儋西上書。

translations.literal: Ti Ying ached at her father's words; how could she shrink from going west to submit a memorial?
translations.idiomatic: Ti Ying was pained by her father's words—how could she shrink from going west to submit her memorial?

sentences.zh: 槃桓北闕下，泣淚何漣如。

translations.literal: She lingered below the northern gate-tower; her weeping tears—how streaming!
translations.idiomatic: She lingered below the northern gate-tower, her tears streaming down.

sentences.zh: 乞得并姊弟，沒身贖父軀。

translations.literal: She begged to have herself and her siblings together, giving her body to redeem her father's person.
translations.idiomatic: She begged to offer herself and her siblings together, giving her life to redeem her father.

sentences.zh: 漢文感其義，肉刑法用除。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han was moved by her righteousness; the corporal punishments were abolished by his act.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han was moved by her devotion and abolished the corporal punishments.

sentences.zh: 其父得以免，辨義在列圖。

translations.literal: Her father thereby escaped punishment; discerning righteousness, she was entered in the rostered pictures.
translations.idiomatic: Her father was spared; her righteous deed was recorded in the illustrated biographies.

sentences.zh: 多男亦何為，一女足成居。

translations.literal: What use are many sons? One daughter was enough to save the household.
translations.idiomatic: What use are many sons? A single daughter was enough to save the household.

sentences.zh: 簡子南渡河，津吏廢舟舩。

translations.literal: Lord Jian crossed the river southward; the ferry officer scrapped the boats.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Jian of Zhao crossed the Yellow River southward; the ferry officer scuttled the boats.

sentences.zh: 執法將加刑，女娟擁櫂前。

translations.literal: The law-enforcers were about to impose punishment; Nü Juan embraced the oar and stepped forward.
translations.idiomatic: The officers were about to punish him when Nü Juan seized the oar and stepped forward.

translations.literal: "My father, hearing that my lord was coming, was about to cross depths of unknown measure.
translations.idiomatic: "My father, hearing that you were coming, was about to cross treacherous waters.

sentences.zh: 畏懼風波起，禱祝祭名川。

translations.literal: Fearing that wind and waves might rise, he prayed and offered sacrifice to the famous rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that wind and waves might rise, he prayed and offered sacrifice to the great rivers.

sentences.zh: 備禮饗神祗，為君求福先。

translations.literal: He prepared rites to feast the spirits, seeking blessings for my lord in advance.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared full rites to honor the spirits and seek blessings on your behalf.

sentences.zh: 不勝釂祀誠，至令犯罰艱。

translations.literal: Unable to bear the fullness of sacrificial sincerity, it led even to violating punishment's hardship.
translations.idiomatic: His overflowing devotion in the rites led him unwittingly to this breach of the law.

sentences.zh: 君必欲加誅，乞使知罪諐。

translations.literal: If my lord must impose execution, I beg that he be made to know his offense and fault.
translations.idiomatic: If you must punish him, I beg that he be told his offense first.

sentences.zh: 妾願以身代」，至誠感蒼天。

translations.literal: This handmaid wishes to substitute her body for his"—utmost sincerity moved azure Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I am willing to take his place"—her utmost sincerity moved Heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 國君高其義，其父用赦原。

translations.literal: The state's lord exalted her righteousness; her father thereby received pardon and release.
translations.idiomatic: The lord of the state honored her righteousness and pardoned her father.

sentences.zh: 河激奏中流，簡子知其賢。

translations.literal: The river surged and music sounded midstream; Jianzi knew her worth.
translations.idiomatic: Music sounded midstream as the river surged; Lord Jian recognized her worth.

sentences.zh: 歸娉為夫人，榮寵超後先。

translations.literal: Returning, he betrothed her as his lady; glory and favor surpassed those before and after.
translations.idiomatic: He took her home as his consort; her honor and favor surpassed all who came before or after.

sentences.zh: 辨女解父命，何況徤少年。

translations.literal: A discerning woman could save her father's life—how much more a robust youth!
translations.idiomatic: If a discerning woman could save her father's life, how much more could a strong young man!

sentences.zh: 黃初發和氣，明堂德教施。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu era harmonious qi arose; in the Bright Hall virtue and teaching were spread.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangchu era harmonious qi arose; in the Bright Hall virtue and teaching were proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 治道致太平，禮樂風俗移。

translations.literal: The Way of governance brought supreme peace; rites and music shifted customs and mores.
translations.idiomatic: The Way of governance brought supreme peace; rites and music transformed the customs of the land.

sentences.zh: 刑錯民無枉，怨女復何為。

translations.literal: Punishments were set aside and the people knew no injustice; what more could resentful women do?
translations.idiomatic: Punishments were set aside and the people knew no injustice—what more could wronged women do?

sentences.zh: 聖皇長壽考，景福常來儀。

translations.literal: May the sage emperor enjoy long life and vigor; bright blessings ever come in their proper forms.
translations.idiomatic: May the sage emperor enjoy long life; bright blessings ever attend him in their proper forms.

translations.literal: "First Month of Winter" — to the tune of "The Cunning Hare."
translations.idiomatic: "First Month of Winter" — to be sung to the tune of "The Cunning Hare."

translations.literal: In the first month of winter, the tenth month—yin qi is stern and clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, the yin force grows stern and clear.

translations.literal: Military officers admonish the hunt; assembled troops marshal the army.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers warn of the hunt; assembled troops marshal the army.

translations.literal: The primordial tortoise inherits auspice; primordial radiance manifests bright.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred tortoise foretells good fortune; primordial light shines forth.

translations.literal: Chiyou clears the road; wind ceases and rain stops.
translations.idiomatic: Chiyou clears the road; wind dies and rain stops.

translations.literal: The imperial carriage sets forth; phoenix bells ring with a deep clatter.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage sets forth; phoenix bells ring with a deep clatter.

translations.literal: Tiger guards and colored riders; flying elephants with ear-pendants of the ha bird.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger guards and colored riders; flying elephants with ear-pendants of the ha bird.

translations.literal: Bells and drums ring resonant; flutes and pipes clamor and call.
translations.idiomatic: Bells and drums ring resonant; flutes and pipes sound in clamorous chorus.

translations.literal: Ten thousand riders level their bits; a thousand chariots match their canopies.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand riders level their bits; a thousand chariots match their canopies.

translations.literal: They level mountains and fill valleys; smooth forests and cleanse marshes.
translations.idiomatic: They level mountains and fill valleys; clear forests and scour the marshes.

translations.literal: Nets are spread for ten thousand li, exhausting all that fly and run.
translations.idiomatic: Nets are spread for ten thousand li, catching all that fly and run.

translations.literal: Flustered, flustered—the cunning hare, raising white fur, leaping with its forelegs.
translations.idiomatic: Flustered, the cunning hare raises its white fur and leaps with its forelegs.

translations.literal: They hunt with blue-feathered bolts; they cover with long poles.
translations.idiomatic: They hunt with blue-feathered bolts and strike with long poles.

translations.literal: Han Lu and Song Que display their talents and stretch their legs.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lu and Song Que display their talents and stretch their legs in the chase.

translations.literal: They bite without exhausting the leash; they drag elk and skewer deer.
translations.idiomatic: They bite without slackening the leash; they drag elk and skewer deer.

translations.literal: Men of Wei release the crossbow mechanism; Yang Ji plucks the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: Men of Wei release the crossbow; Yang Ji draws the bowstring.

translations.literal: Dulu climbers seek the heights, searching out monkeys and apes.
translations.idiomatic: Dulu climbers scale the heights, searching out monkeys and apes.

translations.literal: Qing Ji and Meng Ben tread valleys and leap over peaks.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Ji and Meng Ben tread valleys and leap over mountain peaks.

translations.literal: They widen their eyes and split their corners; in rage they burst through their caps.
translations.idiomatic: They widen their eyes and split their corners; in fury they burst through their caps.

translations.literal: They strike down bears and throttle tigers; they kick leopards and wrestle wild cats.
translations.idiomatic: They strike down bears and throttle tigers; they kick leopards and wrestle wild cats.

translations.literal: Their qi has surplus force; they shoulder elephants and rush forward.
translations.idiomatic: Their strength still overflows; they shoulder elephants and rush forward.

translations.literal: The game carts are already full; the sun inclines and the music ends.
translations.idiomatic: The game carts are full; the sun sinks and the music ends.

translations.literal: Labor is dismissed and troops released; a great feast is held at the detached palace.
translations.idiomatic: The laborers are dismissed and the troops released; a great feast is held at the detached palace.

translations.literal: Envoi:
translations.idiomatic: Envoi:

sentences.zh: 聖皇臨飛軒，論功校獵徒。

translations.literal: The sage emperor faces the flying carriage; he assesses merit and ranks the hunting followers.
translations.idiomatic: The sage emperor faces the flying carriage and ranks the hunters according to their merit.

sentences.zh: 死禽積如京，流血成溝渠。

translations.literal: Dead birds pile like a mound; flowing blood forms ditches and channels.
translations.idiomatic: Dead birds pile like a mound; flowing blood forms ditches and channels.

sentences.zh: 明詔大勞賜，大官供有無。

translations.literal: Bright edicts grant great rewards for labor; the Grand Provisioner supplies what is had and what is not.
translations.idiomatic: Bright edicts grant great rewards; the Grand Provisioner supplies all that is needed.

sentences.zh: 走馬行酒醴，驅車布肉魚。

translations.literal: Running horses carry wine and sweet brew; driven carts spread meat and fish.
translations.idiomatic: Running horses carry wine and sweet brew; driven carts spread meat and fish.

sentences.zh: 鳴鼓舉觴爵，鐘擊位無餘。

translations.literal: Drums sound and goblets are raised; bells strike and no seat remains empty.
translations.idiomatic: Drums sound and goblets are raised; bells strike and every seat is filled.

sentences.zh: 絕網縱麟麑，弛罩出鳳雛。

translations.literal: Nets are cut and unicorn fawns released; covers are slackened and phoenix chicks let out.
translations.idiomatic: Nets are cut and unicorn fawns released; covers are removed and phoenix chicks set free.

sentences.zh: 收功在羽校，威靈振鬼區。

translations.literal: Gathering merit rests with the feathered guard; awe and numen shake the demon regions.
translations.idiomatic: The merit of the hunt rests with the feathered guard; his majesty shakes the realm of spirits.

sentences.zh: 陛下長懽樂，永世合天符。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty long enjoy joy and pleasure; for ten thousand generations accord with Heaven's tally.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty long enjoy joy; for ten thousand generations may he accord with Heaven's mandate.

translations.literal: Jin "Piwu Dance Songs," five pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Five Jin dynasty Battle-Drum Dance songs.

translations.literal: "Great Enterprise" — "Piwu Dance Song."
translations.idiomatic: "Great Enterprise" — a Battle-Drum Dance song.

sentences.zh: 當魏曲《明明魏皇帝》 古曲《關東有賢女》

translations.literal: To the Wei tune "Bright and Illustrious Is the Emperor of Wei"; ancient tune "In the East There Is a Worthy Woman."
translations.idiomatic: To the Wei tune "Bright and Illustrious Is the Emperor of Wei"; ancient tune "In the East There Is a Worthy Woman."

sentences.zh: 宣文剏洪業，盛德在太始。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwen founded the great enterprise; flourishing virtue was in the Taishi era.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwen founded the great enterprise; flourishing virtue began in the Taishi era.

sentences.zh: 聖皇應靈符，受命君四海。

translations.literal: The sage emperor responded to the numinous tally; receiving the mandate, he rules the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: The sage emperor answered to the divine mandate and received Heaven's charge to rule the four seas.

sentences.zh: 萬國何所樂，上有明天子。

translations.literal: What do the ten thousand states rejoice in? Above them is a bright Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: What do the ten thousand states rejoice in? Above them shines the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 唐堯禪帝位，虞舜惟恭己。

translations.literal: Tang Yao ceded the imperial throne; Yu Shun only reverently restrained himself.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yao ceded the throne; Yu Shun only reverently restrained himself.

sentences.zh: 恭己正南面，道化與時移。

translations.literal: Reverently restraining himself, he faced due south; the Way's transformation shifted with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently facing south, he let the Way's transformation shift with the times.

sentences.zh: 大赦盪萌漸，文教被黃支。

translations.literal: Great amnesty washed away sprouting evils; civil teaching covered the Yellow Limbs.
translations.idiomatic: Great amnesty washed away budding evils; civil teaching reached to the farthest lands.

translations.literal: Patterned on Heaven, modeled on Earth—his substance was non-action.
translations.idiomatic: Patterned on Heaven, modeled on Earth—his substance was non-action.

sentences.zh: 聰明配日月，神聖參兩儀。

translations.literal: His intelligence matched sun and moon; his divinity joined the Two Measures.
translations.idiomatic: His intelligence matched sun and moon; his divinity joined Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 雖有三凶類，靜言無所施。

translations.literal: Though there were the three vicious sorts, in stillness he spoke and had nowhere to apply them.
translations.idiomatic: Though the three vicious sorts remained, in his stillness they had no place to act.

translations.literal: Patterned on Heaven, modeled on Earth—his substance was non-action.
translations.idiomatic: Patterned on Heaven, modeled on Earth—his substance was non-action.

sentences.zh: 稷契竝佐命，伊呂升王臣。

translations.literal: Ji and Xie together assisted the mandate; Yi and Lü rose as the king's ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Xie together assisted the mandate; Yi Yin and Lü Shang rose as the king's ministers.

sentences.zh: 蘭芷登朝肆，下無失宿民。

translations.literal: Orchids and angelica entered the court's ranks; below, none lost their settled folk.
translations.idiomatic: Men of worth filled the court; below, none lost their rightful place among the people.

sentences.zh: 聲發響自應，表立景來附。

translations.literal: When sound issued, echoes answered of themselves; when the standard was raised, radiance came to attach.
translations.idiomatic: When sound issued, echoes answered of themselves; when the standard was raised, all came to attach.

sentences.zh: 虓虎從羈制，潛龍升天路。

translations.literal: Fierce tigers followed bridle and restraint; hidden dragons ascended the road to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce tigers submitted to bridle and rein; hidden dragons ascended the road to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 備物立成器，變通極其數。

translations.literal: Preparing things, he established completed vessels; change and penetration reached their numbers' limit.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared all things and established their forms; change and adaptation reached their fullest measure.

sentences.zh: 百事以時敘，萬機有常度。

translations.literal: A hundred affairs were ordered by season; ten thousand mechanisms had constant measures.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred affairs were ordered by season; ten thousand matters had their constant measure.

sentences.zh: 訓之以克讓，納之以忠恕。

translations.literal: He instructed them with overcoming and yielding; he received them with loyalty and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed them in humility and yielding; he received them with loyalty and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 羣下仰清風，海外同懽慕。

translations.literal: The host below looked up to the clear breeze; beyond the seas, all alike rejoiced and admired.
translations.idiomatic: The host below looked up to the clear breeze; beyond the seas, all rejoiced and admired.

translations.literal: Patterned on Heaven, modeled on Earth—his transformation spread like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Patterned on Heaven, modeled on Earth—his transformation spread like clouds.

sentences.zh: 昔日貴雕飾，今尚儉與素。

translations.literal: In former days ornament was prized; now frugality and plainness are honored.
translations.idiomatic: In former days ornament was prized; now frugality and plainness are honored.

sentences.zh: 昔日多纖介，今去情與故。

translations.literal: In former days there was much petty scruple; now feeling and old ties are set aside.
translations.idiomatic: In former days there was much petty scruple; now private feeling and old ties are set aside.

translations.literal: Patterned on Heaven, modeled on Earth—his transformation spread like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Patterned on Heaven, modeled on Earth—his transformation spread like clouds.

sentences.zh: 濟濟大朝士，夙夜綜萬機。

translations.literal: Numerous, numerous—the great court scholars; dawn to dusk they oversee ten thousand mechanisms.
translations.idiomatic: Numerous are the great court scholars; dawn to dusk they oversee ten thousand affairs.

sentences.zh: 萬機無廢理，明明降疇咨。

translations.literal: Of ten thousand mechanisms none were left ungoverned; bright and clear, he descended to confer in fields.
translations.idiomatic: Of ten thousand affairs none were left ungoverned; bright and clear, he descended to seek counsel.

sentences.zh: 臣譬列星景，君配朝日暉。

translations.literal: Ministers are like the arrayed stars' radiance; the lord matches the morning sun's glory.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers are like the arrayed stars; the lord matches the morning sun's glory.

sentences.zh: 事業竝通濟，功烈何巍巍。

translations.literal: Their enterprises together reached full passage; how towering their achievements and merit!
translations.idiomatic: Their enterprises together reached fulfillment; how towering their achievements and merit!

sentences.zh: 五帝繼三皇，三王世所歸。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors succeeded the Three August Ones; the Three Dynasties were what the ages returned to.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors succeeded the Three August Ones; the Three Dynasties were what the ages aspired to.

sentences.zh: 聖德應期運，天地不能違。

translations.literal: Sage virtue answered to the season's fortune; Heaven and Earth could not oppose it.
translations.idiomatic: Sage virtue answered to the season's fortune; Heaven and Earth could not oppose it.

sentences.zh: 仰之彌已高，猶天不可階。

translations.literal: Looking up, it grows ever higher—still like Heaven, without steps to climb.
translations.idiomatic: The more one looks up, the higher it grows—still like Heaven, without steps to climb.

sentences.zh: 將復御龍氏，鳳皇在庭棲。

translations.literal: He will again mount the Dragon Clan; the phoenix perches in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: He will again mount the Dragon Clan; the phoenix perches in the courtyard.

translations.literal: "Heaven's Mandate" — "Piwu Dance Song."
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven's Mandate" — a Battle-Drum Dance song.

sentences.zh: 當魏曲《太和有聖帝》 古曲《章和二年中》

translations.literal: To the Wei tune "In the Taihe Era There Was a Sage Emperor"; ancient tune "In the Second Year of Zhanghe."
translations.idiomatic: To the Wei tune "In the Taihe Era There Was a Sage Emperor"; ancient tune "In the Second Year of Zhanghe."

sentences.zh: 聖祖受天命，應期輔魏皇。

translations.literal: The sage ancestor received Heaven's mandate; answering to the season, he assisted the Wei emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The sage ancestor received Heaven's mandate and, answering to the season, assisted the Wei emperor.

sentences.zh: 入則綜萬機，出則征四方。

translations.literal: Within, he oversaw ten thousand mechanisms; abroad, he campaigned in the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Within, he oversaw ten thousand affairs; abroad, he campaigned in the four directions.

sentences.zh: 朝廷無遺理，方表寧且康。

translations.literal: At court none were left without governance; the regions showed peace and well-being.
translations.idiomatic: At court none were left without governance; the regions showed peace and well-being.

sentences.zh: 道隆舜臣堯，積德踰太王。

translations.literal: His Way towered like Shun serving Yao; accumulated virtue surpassed Great King.
translations.idiomatic: His Way towered like Shun serving Yao; accumulated virtue surpassed that of King Tai.

sentences.zh: 孟度阻窮險，造亂天一隅。

translations.literal: Meng Du blocked desperate passes and raised rebellion in one corner of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Du held desperate passes and raised rebellion in one corner of the realm.

sentences.zh: 神兵出不意，奉命致天誅。

translations.literal: Divine troops issued beyond expectation; receiving the command, they brought Heaven's execution.
translations.idiomatic: Divine troops struck beyond expectation; receiving the command, they brought Heaven's punishment.

sentences.zh: 赦善戮有罪，元惡宗為虛。

translations.literal: They pardoned the good and slew the guilty; the chief villain's clan was reduced to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: They pardoned the good and slew the guilty; the chief villain's clan was reduced to nothing.

sentences.zh: 威風震勁蜀，武烈懾彊吳。

translations.literal: Awe's wind shook sturdy Shu; martial glory awed mighty Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His awe shook sturdy Shu; his martial glory awed mighty Wu.

sentences.zh: 諸葛不知命，肆逆亂天常。

translations.literal: Zhuge did not know his mandate; he wantonly rebelled and disordered Heaven's constants.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang did not know his mandate; he wantonly rebelled and disordered Heaven's constants.

sentences.zh: 擁徒十餘萬，數來寇邊疆。

translations.literal: He mustered followers of more than a hundred thousand; again and again he came raiding the borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered more than a hundred thousand followers and repeatedly raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 我皇邁神武，秉鉞鎮雍涼。

translations.literal: Our emperor surpassed in divine martiality; grasping the battle-axe, he secured Yong and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor, surpassing in divine martial prowess, took the battle-axe and secured Yong and Liang.

sentences.zh: 亮乃畏天威，未戰先仆僵。

translations.literal: Liang then feared Heaven's awe; before battle he already collapsed and stiffened.
translations.idiomatic: Liang then feared Heaven's majesty and, before battle was even joined, collapsed and perished.

sentences.zh: 盈虛自然運，時變固多難。

translations.literal: Fullness and emptiness run by nature's course; as the times shift, hardships are indeed many.
translations.idiomatic: Fullness and emptiness follow nature's course, and as the times turn, hardships abound.

sentences.zh: 東征陵海表，萬里梟賊淵。

translations.literal: On an eastern expedition he crossed the sea's edge; at ten thousand li he beheaded the outlaw Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: On an eastern expedition he crossed beyond the sea and, at ten thousand li, executed the outlaw Yuan.

sentences.zh: 受遺齊七政，曹爽又滔天。

translations.literal: Receiving the testament, he jointly held the seven regencies; Cao Shuang again reached to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the testament, he jointly held the seven regencies, yet Cao Shuang's arrogance again reached to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 羣凶受誅殛，百祿咸來臻。

translations.literal: The band of villains received execution and destruction; the hundred blessings all came to fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: The band of villains were executed and destroyed, and the hundred blessings all arrived in their season.

sentences.zh: 黃華應福始，王淩為禍先。

translations.literal: Yellow splendor answered fortune's beginning; Wang Ling was calamity's harbinger.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow splendor answered the dawn of good fortune, while Wang Ling was the harbinger of calamity.

translations.literal: "Emperor Jing" — "Piwu Dance Song."
translations.idiomatic: "Emperor Jing" — a Battle-Drum Dance song.

sentences.zh: 當魏曲《魏歷長》 古曲《樂久長》

translations.literal: To the Wei tune "Wei's Reign Is Long"; ancient tune "Joy Endures Long."
translations.idiomatic: To the Wei tune "Wei's Reign Is Long"; ancient tune "Joy Endures Long."

sentences.zh: 景皇帝，聰明命世生，盛德參天地。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing—clear and bright, born to command the age; flourishing virtue matched Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing, clear and bright, was born to command the age; his flourishing virtue matched Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 帝王道，創基既已難，繼世亦未易。

translations.literal: The Way of emperors and kings—founding the foundation is already hard; continuing the line is also not easy.
translations.idiomatic: The Way of emperors and kings is hard enough to found, and no less hard to carry on.

sentences.zh: 外則夏侯玄，內則張與李，三凶稱逆，亂帝紀。

translations.literal: Without, Xiahou Xuan; within, Zhang and Li—the three villains proclaimed rebellion and disordered the imperial records.
translations.idiomatic: Without, Xiahou Xuan; within, Zhang and Li—the three villains proclaimed rebellion and disordered the imperial order.

translations.literal: Following Heaven, he carried out execution and exhausted their treachery and hidden plots.
translations.idiomatic: Following Heaven, he carried out punishment and rooted out their treachery to the last.

sentences.zh: 遏將御其漸，潛謀不得起。

translations.literal: He checked the generals and guarded against the beginning; secret plots could not arise.
translations.idiomatic: He checked the generals and guarded against the first stirrings, so secret plots could not arise.

sentences.zh: 罪人咸伏辜，威風震萬里。

translations.literal: The guilty all submitted to punishment; awe's wind shook ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The guilty all submitted to punishment, and his awe shook the realm for ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 平衡綜萬機，萬機無不理。

translations.literal: With balance he oversaw ten thousand mechanisms; of ten thousand mechanisms none were left ungoverned.
translations.idiomatic: With balance he oversaw ten thousand affairs, and of ten thousand affairs none were left ungoverned.

sentences.zh: 召陵桓不君，內外何紛紛，眾小便成羣。

translations.literal: At Shaoling, Huan was no lord; within and without, how chaotic—petty men readily formed factions.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaoling, Huan was no true lord; within and without all was chaos, and petty men readily formed factions.

translations.literal: In darkness and confusion they indulged their hearts; order and disorder they did not distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: In darkness and confusion they indulged their whims and could not tell order from disorder.

translations.literal: Sage Rui decided alone; aiding martial power, he constantly employed culture.
translations.idiomatic: Sage Rui decided alone, aiding martial power by constantly employing civil measures.

sentences.zh: 從天惟廢立，掃霓披浮雲。

translations.literal: Following Heaven alone in deposing and establishing, he swept away rainbows and parted floating clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Following Heaven alone in deposing and establishing rulers, he swept away rainbows and parted the floating clouds.

sentences.zh: 雲霓既已闢，清和未幾間。

translations.literal: Clouds and rainbows having already been cleared, clear harmony had not long to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Once clouds and rainbows were cleared away, clear harmony was not long in coming.

sentences.zh: 羽檄首尾至，變起東南蕃。

translations.literal: Urgent dispatches arrived from first to last; rebellion rose among the southeastern frontier lords.
translations.idiomatic: Urgent dispatches arrived one after another as rebellion rose among the southeastern frontier lords.

sentences.zh: 儉欽為長蛇，外則馮吳蠻。

translations.literal: Jian and Qin formed a long serpent; without, they relied on Wu and the southern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Qin formed a long serpent, and without they relied on Wu and the southern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 萬國紛騷擾，戚戚天下懼不安。

translations.literal: The myriad states were chaotic and disturbed; sorrowful, all under Heaven feared and were not at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The myriad states were thrown into turmoil, and all under Heaven feared in sorrow that peace was lost.

sentences.zh: 神武御六軍，我皇秉鉞征。

translations.literal: With divine martiality he commanded the six armies; our emperor grasped the battle-axe and marched forth.
translations.idiomatic: With divine martiality he commanded the six armies, and our emperor grasped the battle-axe and marched forth.

sentences.zh: 儉欽起壽春，前鋒據項城。

translations.literal: Jian and Qin rose at Shouchun; the vanguard seized Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Qin rose at Shouchun, and their vanguard seized Xiangcheng.

translations.literal: Striking beyond expectation, he together unleashed extraordinary troops.
translations.idiomatic: Striking beyond expectation, he together unleashed extraordinary troops.

sentences.zh: 奇兵誠難御，廟勝實難支。

translations.literal: Extraordinary troops are truly hard to withstand; with victory decided at the temple, they could not in fact hold out.
translations.idiomatic: Extraordinary troops are truly hard to withstand, and with victory already decided at the temple, they could not hold out.

sentences.zh: 兩軍不期遇，敵退計無施。

translations.literal: The two armies met without expectation; the enemy retreated and no stratagem could be applied.
translations.idiomatic: The two armies met without warning; the enemy retreated, and no stratagem availed.

sentences.zh: 虎騎惟武進，大戰沙陽陂。

translations.literal: Tiger cavalry advanced only by martial force; a great battle was fought at Shayang Slope.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger cavalry advanced by martial force alone, and a great battle was fought at Shayang Slope.

sentences.zh: 欽乃亡䰟走，奔虜若雲披。

translations.literal: Qin then lost his soul and fled; the fleeing captives were like clouds parting.
translations.idiomatic: Qin then lost his soul and fled, and the fleeing enemy scattered like clouds parting.

sentences.zh: 天恩赦有辠，東土放鯨鯢。

translations.literal: Heaven's grace pardoned the guilty; in the eastern lands he released the whale and crocodile.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's grace pardoned the guilty, and in the eastern lands he released even the whale and crocodile.

translations.literal: "Great Jin" — "Piwu Dance Song."
translations.idiomatic: "Great Jin" — a Battle-Drum Dance song.

sentences.zh: 當魏曲《天生烝民》 古曲《四方皇》

translations.literal: To the Wei tune "Heaven Bore the Multitudes"; ancient tune "August in the Four Directions."
translations.idiomatic: To the Wei tune "Heaven Bore the Multitudes"; ancient tune "August in the Four Directions."

translations.literal: Illustrious, illustrious Great Jin; solemn and reverent is the Cultured Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Illustrious is Great Jin, and solemn and reverent is the Cultured Emperor.

translations.literal: Vast and towering; his Way surpassed Yao and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Vast and towering, his Way surpassed even Yao and Tang.

sentences.zh: 世稱三皇五帝，及今重其光。

translations.literal: The age praised the Three August Ones and Five Emperors; even now it honors their radiance.
translations.idiomatic: The age praised the Three August Ones and Five Emperors, and even now honors their radiance.

sentences.zh: 九德克明，文既顯武又章。

translations.literal: The nine virtues were fully illumined; culture was already manifest and martial glory also displayed.
translations.idiomatic: The nine virtues were fully illumined; his culture was manifest and his martial glory displayed.

translations.literal: His grace extended through the six directions; he aided all together in the myriad regions.
translations.idiomatic: His grace extended through the six directions and aided all together in the myriad regions.

translations.literal: Within, he raised up the Yuan and Kai; court governance took them as its guiding cord.
translations.idiomatic: Within, he raised up the Yuan and Kai, and court governance took them as its guiding cord.

translations.literal: Without, he selected tiger ministers; in their season they soared like hawks.
translations.idiomatic: Without, he selected tiger ministers who, in their season, soared like hawks.

translations.literal: None who followed failed to come with loyal hearts; those who defied the mandate perished.
translations.idiomatic: None who followed failed to come with loyal hearts, and those who defied the mandate perished.

translations.literal: His benevolence matched the spring sun; his awe surpassed autumn frost.
translations.idiomatic: His benevolence matched the spring sun, and his awe surpassed autumn frost.

translations.literal: Numerous, numerous were the many scholars; together they shared this orchid fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Numerous were the many scholars, sharing together this orchid fragrance.

translations.literal: Tang and Yu reached perfect governance; the four villains reached to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Yu reached perfect governance even when the four villains' evil reached to Heaven.

translations.literal: He sent forces to punish Jian and Qin; none were not reverent and obedient.
translations.idiomatic: He sent forces to punish Jian and Qin, and none failed to submit in reverent obedience.

translations.literal: His transforming influence reached beyond the sea; from beyond the sea guests came.
translations.idiomatic: His transforming influence reached beyond the sea, and from beyond the sea guests came.

translations.literal: They presented their music and song; together they called themselves subject ministers.
translations.idiomatic: They presented their music and song and together declared themselves subject ministers.

translations.literal: Western Shu, crafty toward Xia, usurped titles within its regional domain.
translations.idiomatic: Western Shu, crafty toward the central realm, usurped titles within its regional domain.

translations.literal: He ordered generals to carry out punishment; they surrendered the state and submitted in prostration.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered generals to carry out punishment, and they surrendered the state and submitted in prostration.

translations.literal: The people of Wu defied the mandate; relying on the sea, they blocked the river.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu defied the mandate, relying on the sea to block the river.

translations.literal: Flying dispatches announced and instructed; in response they came to join in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Flying dispatches announced and instructed them, and in response they came to join in harmony.

sentences.zh: 先王建萬國，九服為蕃衛。

translations.literal: The ancient kings established the myriad states; the nine domains served as frontier guards.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings established the myriad states, and the nine domains served as frontier guards.

sentences.zh: 亡秦壞諸侯，序胙不二世。

translations.literal: The fallen Qin destroyed the feudal lords; the order of enfeoffment did not pass two generations.
translations.idiomatic: The fallen Qin destroyed the feudal lords, and the order of enfeoffment did not pass two generations.

sentences.zh: 歷代不能復，忽踰五百歲。

translations.literal: Through successive ages it could not be restored; suddenly more than five hundred years had passed.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive ages it could not be restored, until suddenly more than five hundred years had passed.

sentences.zh: 我皇邁聖德，應期剙典制。

translations.literal: Our emperor surpassed in sage virtue; answering to the season, he founded canonical institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor, surpassing in sage virtue, answered to the season and founded canonical institutions.

translations.literal: He divided the land into five ranks; frontier states had their borders set aright.
translations.idiomatic: He divided the land into five ranks and set aright the borders of the frontier states.

sentences.zh: 莘莘文武佐，千秋遘嘉會。

translations.literal: Numerous civil and martial assistants; through a thousand autumns they met this fine assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Numerous civil and martial assistants met in this fine assembly, a gathering for a thousand autumns.

sentences.zh: 洪業溢區內，仁風翔海外。

translations.literal: The great enterprise overflowed within the realm; the wind of benevolence soared beyond the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The great enterprise overflowed within the realm, and the wind of benevolence soared beyond the sea.

translations.literal: "The Bright Lord" — "Piwu Dance Song."
translations.idiomatic: "The Bright Lord" — a Battle-Drum Dance song.

sentences.zh: 當魏曲《為君既不易》 古曲《殿前生桂樹》

translations.literal: To the Wei tune "Being Lord Is Already Not Easy"; ancient tune "Before the Hall a Cassia Tree Grows."
translations.idiomatic: To the Wei tune "Being Lord Is Already Not Easy"; ancient tune "Before the Hall a Cassia Tree Grows."

sentences.zh: 明君御四海，聽鑑盡物情。

translations.literal: The bright lord ruled the four seas; in listening and judging he exhaustively understood the feelings of things.
translations.idiomatic: The bright lord ruled the four seas, and in listening and judging he understood all things fully.

sentences.zh: 顧望有譴罰，竭忠身必榮。

translations.literal: Those who looked back received censure and punishment; those who exhausted loyalty were surely honored.
translations.idiomatic: Those who looked back received censure and punishment, while those who exhausted their loyalty were surely honored.

sentences.zh: 蘭茝出荒野，萬里升紫庭。

translations.literal: Orchids and angelica came forth from the wild wastes; from ten thousand li they ascended to the purple court.
translations.idiomatic: Orchids and angelica came forth from the wild wastes and, from ten thousand li away, ascended to the purple court.

sentences.zh: 茨草穢堂階，埽截不得生。

translations.literal: Thatch-grass fouled the hall steps; swept and cut off, it could not live.
translations.idiomatic: Thatch-grass fouled the hall steps, but once swept and cut away it could not survive.

sentences.zh: 能否莫相蒙，百官正其名。

translations.literal: Ability and inability were not concealed from one another; the hundred officials had their names set aright.
translations.idiomatic: Ability and inability were not concealed from one another, and the hundred officials had their titles set aright.

sentences.zh: 恭己慎有為，有為無不成。

translations.literal: Reverently restraining himself, he was careful in action; in action, nothing went unaccomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently restraining himself, he was careful in action, and in action nothing went unaccomplished.

sentences.zh: 闇君不自信，羣下執異端。

translations.literal: The dark lord did not trust himself; the multitude below clung to heterodox ways.
translations.idiomatic: The dark lord did not trust himself, and the multitude below clung to heterodox ways.

sentences.zh: 正直罹譖潤，姦臣奪其權。

translations.literal: The upright suffered slander and defilement; wicked ministers seized their authority.
translations.idiomatic: The upright suffered slander and defilement, and wicked ministers seized their authority.

sentences.zh: 雖欲盡忠誠，結舌不敢言。

translations.literal: Though wishing to exhaust loyalty and sincerity, they sealed their tongues and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Though wishing to give their full loyalty, they sealed their tongues and dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 結舌亦何憚，盡忠為身患。

translations.literal: Sealing the tongue—what was there to fear? Exhausting loyalty became a bodily peril.
translations.idiomatic: What was there to fear in sealing the tongue? To exhaust one's loyalty had become a peril to one's person.

sentences.zh: 清流豈不潔，飛塵濁其源。

translations.literal: Is a clear stream not pure? Flying dust muddied its source.
translations.idiomatic: Is a clear stream not pure? Yet flying dust muddied its source.

sentences.zh: 岐路令人迷，未遠勝不還。

translations.literal: Forked roads make men lose their way; not yet far gone, yet better not to return.
translations.idiomatic: Forked roads make men lose their way; though not yet far gone, it is better not to return.

sentences.zh: 忠臣立君朝，正色不顧身。

translations.literal: Loyal ministers stood in the lord's court; with upright countenance they did not regard their persons.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers stood in the lord's court with upright countenance, heedless of their persons.

sentences.zh: 邪正不竝存，譬若胡與秦。

translations.literal: Wickedness and uprightness do not exist together; they are like Hu and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Wickedness and uprightness do not exist together; they are as Hu and Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦胡有合時，邪正各異津。

translations.literal: Qin and Hu had times of meeting; wickedness and uprightness each had different fords.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Hu had times of meeting, but wickedness and uprightness each follow different paths.

sentences.zh: 忠臣遇明君，乾乾惟日新。

translations.literal: Loyal ministers meeting a bright lord—diligent, diligent, only daily renewal.
translations.idiomatic: When loyal ministers meet a bright lord, they are diligent, diligent, renewing themselves day by day.

sentences.zh: 羣目統在綱，眾星拱北辰。

translations.literal: The multitude of eyes were gathered on the guiding cord; the many stars encircled the northern pole.
translations.idiomatic: The multitude of eyes were gathered on the guiding cord, and the many stars encircled the northern pole.

sentences.zh: 設令遭闇主，斥退為凡民。

translations.literal: Suppose one encountered a dark lord—dismissed and sent away, one became a common person.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose one encountered a dark lord: dismissed and sent away, one became a common person.

sentences.zh: 雖薄供時用，白茅猶可珍。

translations.literal: Though meager in supplying timely use, white thatch could still be treasured.
translations.idiomatic: Though meager in supplying timely use, white thatch could still be treasured.

sentences.zh: 氷霜晝夜結，蘭桂摧為薪。

translations.literal: Ice and frost formed day and night; orchids and cassia were broken into firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Ice and frost formed day and night, and orchids and cassia were broken into firewood.

sentences.zh: 邪臣多端變，用心何委曲。

translations.literal: Wicked ministers changed in many ways; how devious were their intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked ministers changed in many ways; how devious were their intentions.

sentences.zh: 便辟從情指，動隨君所欲。

translations.literal: Flatterers followed the lord's inclinations; in movement they followed whatever the lord desired.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers followed the lord's inclinations and in every move followed whatever he desired.

sentences.zh: 偷安樂目前，不問清與濁。

translations.literal: They stole ease and took pleasure in the present moment; they did not ask whether things were clear or muddy.
translations.idiomatic: They stole ease and took pleasure in the present moment, never asking whether things were clear or corrupt.

sentences.zh: 積偽罔時主，養交以持祿。

translations.literal: They piled up falsehood to deceive the lord of the age; they cultivated connections to hold their stipends.
translations.idiomatic: They piled up falsehood to deceive the lord of the age and cultivated connections to hold their stipends.

sentences.zh: 言行恒相違，難饜甚谿谷。

translations.literal: Words and deeds constantly opposed each other; hard to satisfy—deeper than stream valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Words and deeds constantly opposed each other, and their appetite was harder to satisfy than a deep ravine.

sentences.zh: 昧死射乾沒，覺露則滅族。

translations.literal: Risking death they shot at illicit gain; once exposed, their clans were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Risking death they grasped at illicit gain, and once exposed their clans were destroyed.

translations.literal: The five pieces to the right are "Piwu Dance Song" pieces.
translations.idiomatic: The five pieces above are Battle-Drum Dance song texts.

translations.literal: Two song-poems of the "Duo Dance."
translations.idiomatic: Two song-poems of the Bell-Drum Dance.

translations.literal: "The Sage Establishes Rites and Music."
translations.idiomatic: "The Sage Establishes Rites and Music."

sentences.zh: 昔皇文武邪 彌隬舍善 誰吾時吾 行許帝道 銜來治路萬邪 治路萬邪 赫赫 意黃運道吾 治路萬邪 善道明邪金邪 善道 明邪金邪帝邪 近帝武邪武邪 聖皇八音 偶邪尊來 聖皇八音 及來義邪同邪 烏及來義邪 善草供國吾 咄等邪烏 近帝邪武邪 近帝武邪武邪 應節合用 武邪尊邪 應節合用 酒期義邪同邪 酒期義邪 善草供國吾 咄等邪烏 近帝邪武邪 近帝武武邪邪 下音足木 上為鼓義邪 應眾義邪 樂邪邪延否 已邪烏已禮祥 咄等邪烏 素女有絕其聖烏烏武邪

translations.literal: In antiquity the sage kings Wen and Wu (refrain); they broadly gathered and bestowed goodness; who in our age, in our time; walked and upheld the emperor's Way; came bearing governance of the myriad paths (refrain)—governance of the myriad paths (refrain)—glorious, glorious; the intent of the yellow Fortune, the Way (refrain); governance of the myriad paths (refrain); the good Way is bright (refrain), metal (refrain); the good Way, bright (refrain), metal (refrain), emperor (refrain); near the emperor, martial (refrain), martial (refrain); the sage emperor's eight tones; paired (refrain), honored, come; the sage emperor's eight tones; and come, righteousness (refrain), together (refrain); crow and come, righteousness (refrain); good grasses supply the state (refrain); exclaim, and so on (refrain), crow; near the emperor (refrain), martial (refrain); near the emperor, martial (refrain), martial (refrain); matching the beat, joined in use; martial (refrain), honored (refrain); matching the beat, joined in use; at the wine-season, righteousness (refrain), together (refrain); at the wine-season, righteousness (refrain); good grasses supply the state (refrain); exclaim, and so on (refrain), crow; near the emperor (refrain), martial (refrain); near the emperor, martial, martial (refrain), (refrain); below, the tone fills the wooden [instruments]; above, for the drum, righteousness (refrain); responding to the multitude, righteousness (refrain); music (refrain), (refrain), prolonged, no; already (refrain), crow, already rites auspicious; exclaim, and so on (refrain), crow; the Pure Maiden has—cut off—the sage, crow, crow, martial (refrain).
translations.idiomatic: Of old the sage kings Wen and Wu broadly gathered goodness and bestowed it on all; in their season they walked the emperor's Way and opened the myriad paths of rule—paths resounding in glory, bright with Heaven's golden fortune. Clear was the good Way, bright as ringing bronze, nearing the martial virtue of the sage emperor; his eight tones paired in honor, righteousness gathered as one, and good order fed the state. Again the dance neared the emperor's martial glory—foot and hand matching every beat, wine-offering and rite joined as one—lower instruments filling the wood, upper drums calling the multitude; music prolonged the festal order until auspicious rites were complete. Even the Pure Maiden of legend could scarce match the sage's accomplishment in martial harmony.

translations.literal: "Cloud Gate" — "Duo Dance Song" piece.
translations.idiomatic: "Cloud Gate" — a Bell-Drum Dance song text.

translations.literal: To the Wei tune "In the Taihe Era."
translations.idiomatic: To the Wei tune "In the Taihe Era."

sentences.zh: 黃《雲門》，唐《咸池》，虞《韶舞》，夏殷《濩》。

translations.literal: Yellow Emperor's "Cloud Gate," Tang's "Xianchi," Yu's "Shao Dance," Xia and Shang's "Huo."
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor had "Cloud Gate," Tang had "Xianchi," Yu had the "Shao Dance," and Xia and Shang had "Huo."

sentences.zh: 刑代有五，振鐸鳴金，近《大武》。

translations.literal: Form-styles across the ages were five; shaking the clapper and sounding bronze, approaching "Great Martial."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual forms across five ages were five; shaking the clapper and sounding bronze, they approached the "Great Martial" dance.

translations.literal: The clear song leads the chorus; form is master.
translations.idiomatic: The clear song leads the chorus, and the dance form takes the lead.

translations.literal: Sound harmonizes the eight tones; it accords with the pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Sound harmonizes the eight tones and accords with the pitch pipes.

translations.literal: The body does not move without purpose; the hands do not rise in vain.
translations.idiomatic: The body does not move without purpose, nor the hands rise in vain.

translations.literal: Matching the beat and fitting the measure, it completes its sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Matching the beat and fitting the measure, it completes its proper sequence.

translations.literal: At times they played gong and shang, mixing in zhi and yu.
translations.idiomatic: At times they played the gong and shang modes, mixing in zhi and yu.

translations.literal: Below, it fully satisfied the multitude of eyes; above, it followed bells and drums.
translations.idiomatic: Below, it fully satisfied every eye in the crowd; above, it followed the bells and drums.

sentences.zh: 樂以移風，與德禮相輔，安有失其所。

translations.literal: Music transforms the winds of custom; together with virtue and rites it assists—how could there be any losing of its place?
translations.idiomatic: Music transforms the winds of custom and, together with virtue and rites, assists governance—how could it ever lose its proper place?

translations.literal: The two pieces to the right are "Duo Dance Song" pieces.
translations.idiomatic: The two pieces above are Bell-Drum Dance song texts.

translations.literal: Five song-poems of the "Fu Dance."
translations.idiomatic: Five song-poems of the Whisk Dance.

translations.literal: "White Dove."
translations.idiomatic: "White Dove."

translations.literal: Gracefully, gracefully—the white dove; again it flies, again it cries.
translations.idiomatic: Gracefully, gracefully, the white dove flies and cries again and again.

translations.literal: Cherishing my lord's virtue, it came to gather in the lord's courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Cherishing my lord's virtue, it came to gather in his courtyard.

translations.literal: The white sparrow presented auspicious omen; its plain feathers bright and fresh.
translations.idiomatic: The white sparrow presented an auspicious omen, its plain feathers bright and fresh.

translations.literal: Soaring in the courtyard, dancing its wings, to respond to benevolent Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Soaring in the courtyard and dancing its wings, it answered benevolent Heaven.

translations.literal: Chirping, chirping—the calling dove, now red, now yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Chirping, chirping, the calling dove, now red, now yellow.

translations.literal: Delighting in my lord's grace, it ruffled its wings and came soaring.
translations.idiomatic: Delighting in my lord's grace, it ruffled its wings and came soaring.

translations.literal: Light remaining at the eastern wall; fish are in the rivers and lakes.
translations.idiomatic: Light lingers at the eastern wall, and fish swim in the rivers and lakes.

translations.literal: Grace without expense; he honored my humble person.
translations.idiomatic: His grace cost nothing, yet he honored my humble person.

translations.literal: He drove my fine team of four; he trained me in racing and galloping.
translations.idiomatic: He drove my fine team of four and trained me in racing and galloping.

translations.literal: Turning about with my lord, I rejoiced in the Way without remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Turning about with my lord, I rejoiced in the Way without end.

translations.literal: My heart was empty and still; my will was soaked and nourished.
translations.idiomatic: My heart was empty and still, and my will was soaked and nourished.

translations.literal: Playing zither and striking se—just to amuse myself.
translations.idiomatic: Playing zither and striking se, just to amuse myself.

translations.literal: Ascending the Cloud-Tower Terrace, floating and roaming in the Great Clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Ascending the Cloud-Tower Terrace, I floated and roamed in the Great Clarity.

translations.literal: Clasping the dragon and attaching to the phoenix, day by day I hoped my body would grow light.
translations.idiomatic: Clasping the dragon and attaching to the phoenix, day by day I hoped my body would grow light.

translations.literal: "Numerous."
translations.idiomatic: "Numerous."

translations.literal: Freely flying, freely dancing; breath flows fragrant.
translations.idiomatic: Freely flying, freely dancing, breath flows fragrant.

translations.literal: Recalling the Three and Five; great splendor, golden yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, great splendor, golden and bright.

translations.literal: What goes and what is lost, what is gained—the season can be acted upon.
translations.idiomatic: What goes and what is lost, what is gained—the season can still be seized.

translations.literal: Going and coming at the same time—this has not yet reached its end.
translations.idiomatic: Going and coming at the same time—this has not yet reached its end.

translations.literal: The season slowly fades; mulberry and elm are near.
translations.idiomatic: The season slowly fades, and mulberry and elm draw near.

translations.literal: One should only drink wine and take joy in merriment.
translations.idiomatic: One should only drink wine and take joy in merriment.

translations.literal: Age and decay pass away—what deadline is there?
translations.idiomatic: Age and decay pass away—what deadline can one set?

translations.literal: Many worries, bright and burning; within, the heart harbors longing.
translations.idiomatic: Many worries burn bright within, and the heart harbors deep longing.

translations.literal: The deep pool is broad; fish alone are scarce.
translations.idiomatic: The deep pool is broad, yet fish are scarce.

translations.literal: I wish to obtain the yellow bank; the multitude relies upon it.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to reach the yellow bank where the multitude relies.

translations.literal: Grace moves people; in the world there is none to compare.
translations.idiomatic: Grace moves people as none in the world can compare.

translations.literal: Mournful song complete with dance—without limit, it ends.
translations.idiomatic: Mournful song complete with dance—without limit, it ends.

translations.literal: "Dulu."
translations.idiomatic: "Dulu."

translations.literal: Dulu, dulu—the water is deep and the mud is foul.
translations.idiomatic: Dulu, dulu—the water is deep and the mud is foul.

translations.literal: Foul mud one can still bear; deep water kills me.
translations.idiomatic: Foul mud one can still bear, but deep water kills me.

translations.literal: Harmonious, harmonious—a pair of wild geese, sporting at the field's edge.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonious, harmonious—a pair of wild geese sporting at the field's edge.

translations.literal: Civil institutions at its center; martial not exhausting martial—moving the army, swearing the host; ritual complete, then righteous action.
translations.idiomatic: Civil institutions at its center; martial not exhausting martial—moving the army, swearing the host; ritual complete, then righteous action.

sentences.zh: 三驅以崇仁，進止不失其序。

translations.literal: Three-sided drive to exalt benevolence; advance and halt never losing their order.
translations.idiomatic: Three-sided drive to exalt benevolence; advance and halt never losing their order.

translations.literal: Soldiers and troops drilled; generals like tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and troops drilled; generals like tigers.

translations.literal: Only roaring tigers—spirit towering over azure clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Only roaring tigers—spirit towering over azure clouds.

translations.literal: Opening the encirclement on three sides; killing without exterminating the flock.
translations.idiomatic: Opening the encirclement on three sides; killing without exterminating the flock.

translations.literal: Lowering banners and flags; distributing among the six armies.
translations.idiomatic: Lowering banners and flags; distributing among the six armies.

translations.literal: Presenting offerings at the steam-sacrifice; restoring canonical civil texts.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting offerings at the steam-sacrifice; restoring canonical civil texts.

translations.literal: Praising Great Jin—virtue matching Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Praising Great Jin—virtue matching Heaven.

translations.literal: Stipends repaid merit; ranks awaited the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Stipends repaid merit; ranks awaited the worthy.

sentences.zh: 饗燕樂，受茲百祿，嘉萬年。

translations.literal: Feasting in banquet joy; receiving these hundred blessings—fine for ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Feasting in banquet joy; receiving these hundred blessings—fine for ten thousand years.
