translations.literal: "Wulin"[1]
translations.idiomatic: "Wulin"[1]

sentences.zh: 《烏林》者，言曹操既破荊州，從流東下，欲來爭鋒。

translations.literal: "Wulin" speaks of Cao Cao, having broken Jing province, following the current eastward—wishing to come and contend for mastery.
translations.idiomatic: "Wulin" tells how Cao Cao, after conquering Jing province, sailed downstream to the east intent on a decisive clash.

sentences.zh: 大皇帝命將周瑜逆擊之於烏林而破走也。

translations.literal: The Great Emperor ordered the general Zhou Yu to strike back at Wulin and rout him.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Emperor ordered Zhou Yu to meet him at Wulin, where he was defeated and driven off.

sentences.zh: 漢曲有《上之回》，此篇當之第四。

translations.literal: Among Han pieces there is "Shang zhi Hui"; this piece corresponds as the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Among Han pieces there is "Shang zhi Hui"; this piece corresponds as the fourth.

translations.literal: Cao Cao campaigned north; took Willow City.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao campaigned north; took Willow City.

translations.literal: Riding victory, sweeping all before him; then campaigning south.
translations.idiomatic: Riding victory, sweeping all before him; then campaigning south.

translations.literal: The Liu house was not at peace; eight commanderies shook in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu house was not at peace; eight commanderies shook in alarm.

translations.literal: The masses having surrendered, Cao slaughtered Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The masses having surrendered, Cao slaughtered Jing.

translations.literal: Ships and chariots a hundred thousand; raising wind and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Ships and chariots a hundred thousand; raising wind and fame.

translations.literal: Counselors were fox-like in doubt; fearing no success.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors were fox-like in doubt; fearing no success.

translations.literal: Relying on our Great Emperor; issuing sage clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on our Great Emperor; issuing sage clarity.

translations.literal: Tiger ministers, heroic and fierce—Zhou and Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger ministers, heroic and fierce—Zhou and Cheng.

translations.literal: Breaking Cao at Wulin; displaying and proclaiming merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Breaking Cao at Wulin; displaying and proclaiming merit and fame.

sentences.zh: 右《伐烏林》曲，凡十八句，其十句句四字，八句句三字。

translations.literal: Above: the "Campaigning at Wulin" piece—in all eighteen lines; ten lines of four characters each, eight lines of three characters each.
translations.idiomatic: Above: the "Campaigning at Wulin" piece—in all eighteen lines; ten lines of four characters each, eight lines of three characters each.

translations.literal: "Autumn Wind"[1]
translations.idiomatic: "Autumn Wind"[1]

sentences.zh: 《秋風》者，言大皇帝說以使民，民忘其死。

translations.literal: "Autumn Wind" speaks of the Great Emperor persuading to employ the people—the people forgot their death.
translations.idiomatic: "Autumn Wind" tells how the Great Emperor moved the people with his words until they forgot the fear of death.

sentences.zh: 漢曲有《{扌雝}離》，此篇當之。

translations.literal: Among Han pieces there is "Yong Li"; this piece corresponds.
translations.idiomatic: Among Han pieces there is "Yong Li"; this piece corresponds.

translations.literal: Fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth.

sentences.zh: 秋風揚沙塵，寒露霑衣裳。

translations.literal: Autumn wind raised sand and dust; cold dew wet the garments.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn wind raised sand and dust; cold dew wet the garments.

sentences.zh: 角弓持弦急，鳩鳥化為鷹。

translations.literal: Horn bows held, strings tight; turtledoves transformed into hawks.
translations.idiomatic: Horn bows held, strings tight; turtledoves transformed into hawks.

sentences.zh: 邊垂飛羽檄，寇賊侵界疆。

translations.literal: On the frontier, urgent dispatches flew; bandits and raiders invaded the borders.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier, urgent dispatches flew; bandits and raiders invaded the borders.

sentences.zh: 跨馬披介胄，慷慨懷悲傷。

translations.literal: Mounting horses, donning armor; ardent in spirit, harboring grief.
translations.idiomatic: Mounting horses, donning armor; ardent in spirit, harboring grief.

sentences.zh: 辭親向長路，安知存與亡。

translations.literal: Bidding farewell to kin, facing the long road—who knows life or death?
translations.idiomatic: Bidding farewell to kin, facing the long road—who knows life or death?

sentences.zh: 窮達固有分，志士思立功。

translations.literal: Adversity and success have their allotted share; men of resolve think to establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: Adversity and success have their allotted share; men of resolve think to establish merit.

sentences.zh: 邀之戰場，身逸獲高賞，身沒有遺封。

translations.literal: Summoned to the battlefield—if the body survives, high reward; if the body perishes, posthumous enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the battlefield—if the body survives, high reward; if the body perishes, posthumous enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 右《秋風》曲，凡十五句，其十四句句五字，一句四字。

translations.literal: Above: the "Autumn Wind" piece—in all fifteen lines; fourteen lines of five characters each, one line of four characters.
translations.idiomatic: Above: the "Autumn Wind" piece—in all fifteen lines; fourteen lines of five characters each, one line of four characters.

translations.literal: "Taking Wancheng"[1]
translations.idiomatic: "Taking Wancheng"[1]

sentences.zh: 《克皖城》者，言曹操志圖并兼，而令朱光為廬江太守。

translations.literal: "Taking Wancheng" speaks of Cao Cao's intent to annex and merge—appointing Zhu Guang as Administrator of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: "Taking Wancheng" tells how Cao Cao sought to annex the realm and installed Zhu Guang as Administrator of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 上親征光，破之於皖城也。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally campaigned against Guang; broke him at Wancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor personally campaigned against Guang and defeated him at Wancheng.

sentences.zh: 漢曲有《戰城南》，此篇當之第六。

translations.literal: Among Han pieces there is "Fighting South of the Wall"; this piece corresponds as the sixth.
translations.idiomatic: Among Han pieces there is "Fighting South of the Wall"; this piece corresponds as the sixth.

translations.literal: Conquering and destroying Wancheng; checking bandits and raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Conquering and destroying Wancheng; checking bandits and raiders.

translations.literal: Hating these villainous spawn; blocking treachery and wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Hating these villainous spawn; blocking treachery and wickedness.

translations.literal: Royal troops blazed in campaign; the host overturned.
translations.idiomatic: Royal troops blazed in campaign; the host overturned.

translations.literal: Removing filth, banishing violence; sheathing arms and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Removing filth, banishing violence; sheathing arms and armor.

translations.literal: The people could return to farming; the borders rested.
translations.idiomatic: The people could return to farming; the borders rested.

translations.literal: Punishing the lord, comforting the ministers—displaying utmost virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing the lord, comforting the ministers—displaying utmost virtue.

sentences.zh: 右《克皖城》曲，凡十二句，其六句句三字，六句句四字。

translations.literal: Above: the "Taking Wancheng" piece—in all twelve lines; six lines of three characters each, six lines of four characters each.
translations.idiomatic: Above: the "Taking Wancheng" piece—in all twelve lines; six lines of three characters each, six lines of four characters each.

translations.literal: "Guan Betrays Virtue"[1]
translations.idiomatic: "Guan Betrays Virtue"[1]

sentences.zh: 《關背德》者，言蜀將關羽背棄吳德，心懷不軌。

translations.literal: "Guan Betrays Virtue" speaks of Shu general Guan Yu abandoning Wu's virtue—harboring rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: "Guan Betrays Virtue" tells how the Shu general Guan Yu cast off Wu's goodwill and harbored treasonous designs.

sentences.zh: 大皇帝引師浮江而禽之也。

translations.literal: The Great Emperor led troops across the river and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Emperor led troops across the river and captured him.

sentences.zh: 漢曲有《巫山高》，此篇當之第七。

translations.literal: Among Han pieces there is "Wushan High"; this piece corresponds as the seventh.
translations.idiomatic: Among Han pieces there is "Wushan High"; this piece corresponds as the seventh.

translations.literal: Guan betrayed virtue; acting like an owl spreading its wings.
translations.idiomatic: Guan betrayed virtue; acting like an owl spreading its wings.

translations.literal: Carving off our towns and cities; plotting ill omens.
translations.idiomatic: Carving off our towns and cities; plotting ill omens.

translations.literal: Raising arms, campaigning north; besieging Fan and Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Raising arms, campaigning north; besieging Fan and Xiangyang.

translations.literal: Alas—the arm larger than the thigh; he would receive its calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—the arm larger than the thigh; he would receive its calamity.

sentences.zh: 巍巍吳聖主，叡德與玄通。

translations.literal: Lofty, lofty Wu's sage lord—sagely virtue joined with the dark and mysterious.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty, lofty Wu's sage lord—sagely virtue joined with the dark and mysterious.

translations.literal: Joined with the dark and mysterious; personally trusting Lü Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Joined with the dark and mysterious; personally trusting Lü Meng.

translations.literal: Floating boats on Hongsi Pool; crossing the long Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Floating boats on Hongsi Pool; crossing the long Yangtze.

translations.literal: How mighty, how imposing the divine martial bearing!
translations.idiomatic: How mighty, how imposing the divine martial bearing!

translations.literal: Fame and glory just then soared with the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Fame and glory just then soared with the wind.

translations.literal: Passing through and pacifying Jiang'an city; greatly holding the Ying domain.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through and pacifying Jiang'an city; greatly holding the Ying domain.

sentences.zh: 虜羽授首，百蠻咸來同，盛哉無比隆。

translations.literal: The captive Yu surrendered his head; the hundred barbarians all came in unity—how flourishing, none could match its height.
translations.idiomatic: The captive Yu surrendered his head; the hundred barbarians all came in unity—how flourishing, none could match its height.

sentences.zh: 右《關背德》曲，凡二十一句，其八句句四字，二句句六字，七句句五字，四句句三字。

translations.literal: Above: the "Guan Betrays Virtue" piece—in all twenty-one lines; eight lines of four characters, two lines of six characters, seven lines of five characters, four lines of three characters.
translations.idiomatic: Above: the "Guan Betrays Virtue" piece—in all twenty-one lines; eight lines of four characters, two lines of six characters, seven lines of five characters, four lines of three characters.

translations.literal: "Opening Jingmen"[1]
translations.idiomatic: "Opening Jingmen"[1]

sentences.zh: 《通荊門》者，言大皇帝與蜀交好齊盟，中有關羽自失之愆，戎蠻樂亂，生變作患，蜀疑其眩，吳惡其詐，乃大治兵，終復初好也。

translations.literal: "Opening Jingmen" speaks of the Great Emperor exchanging goodwill and forming alliance with Shu—amid which Guan Yu's self-caused fault, barbarians delighting in chaos, change arising and becoming disaster; Shu suspected deception, Wu hated treachery—then greatly ordering troops, at last restoring the original friendship.
translations.idiomatic: "Opening Jingmen" recounts how the Great Emperor allied with Shu until Guan Yu's own error, barbarian unrest, and mutual suspicion between the two states forced a great mobilization—yet in the end their original friendship was restored.

sentences.zh: 漢曲有《上陵》，此篇當之第八。

translations.literal: Among Han pieces there is "Ascending the Mound"; this piece corresponds as the eighth.
translations.idiomatic: Among Han pieces there is "Ascending the Mound"; this piece corresponds as the eighth.

sentences.zh: 荊門限巫山，高峻與雲連。

translations.literal: Jingmen bounded by Wushan—high and steep, joined with clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmen bounded by Wushan—high and steep, joined with clouds.

sentences.zh: 蠻夷阻其險，歷世懷不賓。

translations.literal: Barbarians blocked its peril; through generations harbored refusal to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians blocked its peril; through generations harbored refusal to submit.

sentences.zh: 漢王據蜀郡，崇好結和親。

translations.literal: The Han king held Shu commandery; exalted friendship, forming marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: The Han king held Shu commandery; exalted friendship, forming marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 乖微中情疑，讒夫亂其間。

translations.literal: Discord subtle, hearts within suspected; slanderers stirred chaos between them.
translations.idiomatic: Discord subtle, hearts within suspected; slanderers stirred chaos between them.

sentences.zh: 大皇赫斯怒，虎臣勇氣震。

translations.literal: The Great Emperor blazed thus in wrath; tiger ministers, courage shaking.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Emperor blazed thus in wrath; tiger ministers, courage shaking.

translations.literal: Scouring dark thickets; punishing the disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: Scouring dark thickets; punishing the disrespectful.

sentences.zh: 觀兵揚炎燿，厲鋒整封疆。

translations.literal: Reviewing troops, raising blazing glory; sharpening blades, ordering the frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing troops, raising blazing glory; sharpening blades, ordering the frontiers.

translations.literal: Ordering the frontiers; spreading martial awe and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Ordering the frontiers; spreading martial awe and bearing.

translations.literal: Merit blazing and glorious; great glory shining and displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Merit blazing and glorious; great glory shining and displayed.

sentences.zh: 邈矣帝皇世，聖吳同厥風。

translations.literal: Remote the age of emperors and kings; sage Wu shares its wind.
translations.idiomatic: Remote the age of emperors and kings; sage Wu shares its wind.

translations.literal: Wild frontiers looked to clear transformation; transformation vast and grand.
translations.idiomatic: Wild frontiers looked to clear transformation; transformation vast and grand.

translations.literal: Blazing, blazing Great Wu; extending fortune forever without end.
translations.idiomatic: Blazing, blazing Great Wu; extending fortune forever without end.

sentences.zh: 右《通荊門》曲，凡二十四句，其十七句句五字，四句句三字，三句句四字。

translations.literal: Above: the "Opening Jingmen" piece—in all twenty-four lines; seventeen lines of five characters, four lines of three characters, three lines of four characters.
translations.idiomatic: Above: the "Opening Jingmen" piece—in all twenty-four lines; seventeen lines of five characters, four lines of three characters, three lines of four characters.

translations.literal: "Displaying Great Virtue"[1]
translations.idiomatic: "Displaying Great Virtue"[1]

sentences.zh: 《章洪德》者，言大皇帝章其大德，而遠方來附也。

translations.literal: "Displaying Great Virtue" speaks of the Great Emperor displaying his great virtue—distant regions coming to attach.
translations.idiomatic: "Displaying Great Virtue" tells how the Great Emperor proclaimed his great virtue until distant lands came to submit.

sentences.zh: 漢曲有《將進酒》，此篇當之第九。

translations.literal: Among Han pieces there is "Bring in the Wine"; this piece corresponds as the ninth.
translations.idiomatic: Among Han pieces there is "Bring in the Wine"; this piece corresponds as the ninth.

translations.literal: Displaying great virtue; surpassing awe and numen.
translations.idiomatic: Displaying great virtue; surpassing awe and numen.

translations.literal: Moved by diverse winds; cherishing distant neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by diverse winds; cherishing distant neighbors.

translations.literal: Pacifying the southern frontier; aligning the sea's edge.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying the southern frontier; aligning the sea's edge.

translations.literal: Yuechang offered tribute; Funan became subject.
translations.idiomatic: Yuechang offered tribute; Funan became subject.

translations.literal: Precious goods filled the court; what was seen daily renewed.
translations.idiomatic: Precious goods filled the court; what was seen daily renewed.

sentences.zh: 右《章洪德》曲，凡十句，其八句句三字，二句句四字。

translations.literal: Above: the "Displaying Great Virtue" piece—in all ten lines; eight lines of three characters, two lines of four characters.
translations.idiomatic: Above: the "Displaying Great Virtue" piece—in all ten lines; eight lines of three characters, two lines of four characters.

translations.literal: "Following the Calendar's Count"[1]
translations.idiomatic: "Following the Calendar's Count"[1]

sentences.zh: 《從歷數》者，言大皇帝從籙圖之符，而建大號也。

translations.literal: "Following the Calendar's Count" speaks of the Great Emperor following the tally and chart's token—establishing the great title.
translations.idiomatic: "Following the Calendar's Count" tells how the Great Emperor answered to Heaven's tally and chart and proclaimed the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 漢曲有《有所思》，此篇當之第十。

translations.literal: Among Han pieces there is "I Have One I Think Of"; this piece corresponds as the tenth.
translations.idiomatic: Among Han pieces there is "I Have One I Think Of"; this piece corresponds as the tenth.

translations.literal: Following the calendar's count—how solemn our emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Following the calendar's count—how solemn our emperor.

sentences.zh: 聖哲受之天，神明表奇異。

translations.literal: Sage and wise, receiving it from Heaven; spirits bright displayed marvels.
translations.idiomatic: Sage and wise, receiving it from Heaven; spirits bright displayed marvels.

sentences.zh: 建號剙皇基，聰叡協神思。

translations.literal: Establishing the title, founding the imperial foundation; clear and wise, accorded with divine thought.
translations.idiomatic: Establishing the title, founding the imperial foundation; clear and wise, accorded with divine thought.

sentences.zh: 德澤浸及昆蟲，浩蕩越前代。

translations.literal: Virtue's blessing soaked even to insects; vast and overflowing, surpassing former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue's blessing soaked even to insects; vast and overflowing, surpassing former ages.

sentences.zh: 三光顯精燿，陰陽稱至治。

translations.literal: The three luminaries displayed refined radiance; yin and yang proclaimed utmost governance.
translations.idiomatic: The three luminaries displayed refined radiance; yin and yang proclaimed utmost governance.

sentences.zh: 肉角步郊畛，鳳凰棲靈囿。

translations.literal: Horned beasts walked the suburban fields; phoenixes roosted in the sacred park.
translations.idiomatic: Horned beasts walked the suburban fields; phoenixes roosted in the sacred park.

sentences.zh: 神龜游沼池，圖讖摹文字。

translations.literal: Divine turtles swam in marsh pools; charts and prophecies traced their characters.
translations.idiomatic: Divine turtles swam in marsh pools; charts and prophecies traced their characters.

translations.literal: Yellow dragon appeared, showing its scales; tokens and omens recorded by sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow dragon appeared, showing its scales; tokens and omens recorded by sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 覽往以察今，我皇多噲事。

translations.literal: Surveying the past to examine the present—our emperor has many sagely undertakings.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying the past to examine the present—our emperor has many sagely undertakings.

sentences.zh: 上欽昊天象，下副萬姓意。

translations.literal: Above, revering Grand Heaven's signs; below, matching the myriad surnames' intent.
translations.idiomatic: Above, revering Grand Heaven's signs; below, matching the myriad surnames' intent.

sentences.zh: 光被彌蒼生，家戶蒙惠賚。

translations.literal: Glory covering all living beings; every household received gracious bounty.
translations.idiomatic: Glory covering all living beings; every household received gracious bounty.

sentences.zh: 風教肅以平，頌聲章嘉喜。

translations.literal: Wind and teaching solemn yet peaceful; praise-sounds displayed joy and delight.
translations.idiomatic: Wind and teaching solemn yet peaceful; praise-sounds displayed joy and delight.

translations.literal: Great Wu flourished and rose; abundantly with surplus ease.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wu flourished and rose; abundantly with surplus ease.

sentences.zh: 右《從歷數》曲，凡二十六句，其一句句三字，三句句四字，二十二句句五字，一句六字。

translations.literal: Above: the "Following the Calendar's Count" piece—in all twenty-six lines; one line of three characters, three lines of four characters, twenty-two lines of five characters, one line of six characters.
translations.idiomatic: Above: the "Following the Calendar's Count" piece—in all twenty-six lines; one line of three characters, three lines of four characters, twenty-two lines of five characters, one line of six characters.

translations.literal: "Receiving Heaven's Mandate"[1]
translations.idiomatic: Receiving Heaven's Mandate

sentences.zh: 《承天命》者，言上以聖德踐位，道化至德盛也。

translations.literal: "Receiving Heaven's Mandate" speaks of the emperor above treading the throne through sage virtue—the Way's transforming power, utmost virtue flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: "Receiving Heaven's Mandate" celebrates the emperor's accession through sage virtue, until the Way's transforming power reached its fullest height.

sentences.zh: 漢曲有《芳樹》，此篇當之第十一。

translations.literal: Among Han pieces there is "Fragrant Trees"; this piece corresponds as the eleventh.
translations.idiomatic: This piece corresponds to Han's "Fragrant Trees" as the eleventh.

translations.literal: Receiving Heaven's mandate—how solemn the sage virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate received—how deep and solemn the sage virtue.

translations.literal: The three essences lowered their signs; tokens and numen displayed virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The three essences sent down their signs; portents and numen proclaimed his virtue.

translations.literal: Giant stones stood; nine ears of grain planted.
translations.idiomatic: Monoliths rose from the earth; nine-eared grain sprang up.

translations.literal: Dragons golden in their scales; crows crimson in their hue.
translations.idiomatic: Dragons sheathed in gold scales; crows bright with crimson plumage.

translations.literal: Cart-drivers sang; a hundred million men sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Men in the streets sang; a hundred million voices sighed as one.

translations.literal: Surpassing the dragon, ascending; inheriting the imperial robes.
translations.idiomatic: He rose above the dragon and ascended, taking up the imperial robes.

translations.literal: In person pure and excellent; embodying the dark and silent.
translations.idiomatic: Pure in bearing, excellent in conduct; he embodied the dark Way in silence.

translations.literal: Rising early to attend court; toiling in humility until the sun slanted.
translations.idiomatic: He rose before dawn for court, laboring in humility until the sun stood low.

sentences.zh: 易簡以崇仁，放遠讒與慝。

translations.literal: Easy and simple to exalt benevolence; banishing far slander and wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Through ease and simplicity he exalted benevolence, driving slander and wickedness far away.

translations.literal: Raising worthy talent; drawing near the virtuous.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the worthy and drew close to men of virtue.

translations.literal: Equalizing fields; flourishing grain and harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Fields were equalized; grain and harvest flourished.

translations.literal: Examining laws and decrees; fixing ranks and forms.
translations.idiomatic: Laws and decrees were examined; ranks and forms were fixed.

translations.literal: Assessing merit and function; clarifying demotion and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Merit and office were weighed; promotion and demotion made clear.

translations.literal: People thought to exhaust themselves—only heart and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Each person gave his utmost—heart and strength together.

translations.literal: House and state governed; the kingly Way straight.
translations.idiomatic: House and state were well governed; the kingly Way ran straight.

translations.literal: Thinking of our emperor—life for ten thousand millions.
translations.idiomatic: We pray for our emperor—ten thousand millions of years of life.

translations.literal: Long preserving Heaven's blessing; sacrificial meat without limit.
translations.idiomatic: May he long keep Heaven's blessing; may sacrificial bounty never end.

sentences.zh: 右《承天命》曲，凡三十四句，其十九句句三字，二句句五字，十三句句四字。

translations.literal: Above: the "Receiving Heaven's Mandate" piece—in all thirty-four lines; nineteen lines of three characters, two lines of five characters, thirteen lines of four characters.
translations.idiomatic: Above: "Receiving Heaven's Mandate"—thirty-four lines total.

translations.literal: "Dark Transformation"[1]
translations.idiomatic: Dark Transformation

sentences.zh: 《玄化》者，言上修文訓武，則天而行，仁澤流洽，天下喜樂也。

translations.literal: "Dark Transformation" speaks of the emperor above cultivating civil teaching and martial training—acting as Heaven ordains; benevolent blessing flowing and reaching; all under Heaven rejoicing.
translations.idiomatic: "Dark Transformation" tells how the emperor cultivated civil and martial arts, followed Heaven's way, spread benevolent grace, and brought joy to all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 漢曲有《上邪》，此篇當之第十二。

translations.literal: Among Han pieces there is "Shang Ye"; this piece corresponds as the twelfth.
translations.idiomatic: This piece corresponds to Han's "Shang Ye" as the twelfth.

translations.literal: Dark transformation mirrored Heaven; Your Majesty sage and true.
translations.idiomatic: Dark transformation took Heaven as its model; Your Majesty, sage and true.

translations.literal: Spreading the imperial cords; leading the Way to settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: He spread the imperial net and led the Way to settle the people.

sentences.zh: 惠澤宣流而雲布，上下睦親。

translations.literal: Gracious blessing proclaimed and flowing like clouds spread; above and below harmonious and close.
translations.idiomatic: Gracious blessing poured forth like clouds; above and below lived in harmony.

sentences.zh: 君臣酣宴樂，激發弦歌揚妙新。

translations.literal: Lord and ministers feasted in joy; stirring strings and songs, raising subtle novelty.
translations.idiomatic: Lord and ministers feasted in delight; strings and songs rang out with fresh grace.

sentences.zh: 脩文籌廟勝，須時備駕廵洛津。

translations.literal: Cultivating civil arts, planning victory in the temple; awaiting the season, preparing the carriage to tour Luoyang's ford.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated civil arts and planned victory in the temple, then at the proper season prepared to tour Luoyang's ford.

sentences.zh: 康哉泰，四海歡忻，越與三五鄰。

translations.literal: How peaceful and great; the four seas rejoiced—surpassing, neighbor to the Three and Five.
translations.idiomatic: How peaceful, how great—the four seas rejoiced; he stood beside the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 右《玄化》曲，凡十三句，其五句句五字，二句句三字，三句句四字，三句句七字。

translations.literal: Above: the "Dark Transformation" piece—in all thirteen lines; five lines of five characters, two lines of three characters, three lines of four characters, three lines of seven characters.
translations.idiomatic: Above: "Dark Transformation"—thirteen lines total.

translations.literal: Present drum-and-fife nao song lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: Current nao song lyrics for drum-and-fife music.

sentences.zh: 〈樂人以音聲相傳，訓詁不可復解。〉

translations.literal: 〈Musicians transmitted these by sound alone; the glosses can no longer be recovered.〉
translations.idiomatic: The musicians handed these down by sound alone; the old glosses can no longer be parsed.

translations.literal: "Shang Ye Piece"[1]
translations.idiomatic: Shang Ye Piece

sentences.zh: 大竭夜烏自雲何來堂吾來聲烏奚姑悟姑尊盧聖子黃尊來餭清嬰烏白日為隨來郭吾微令吾

translations.literal: Great exhaustion, night crow—from what cloud does it come? Hall (refrain), come, voice crow—what maiden? Enlightened maiden, Zun Lu, sage child yellow, honored come, offering clear, infant crow, white sun as following come, Guo (refrain), slight (refrain).
translations.idiomatic: Through the deep night a crow calls from the clouds; honored sages of old descend with bright offerings, and the white sun follows in their train—a festal refrain rising and falling on the wind.

sentences.zh: 應龍夜烏由道何來直子為烏奚如悟姑尊盧雞子聽烏虎行為來明吾微令吾

translations.literal: Responding dragon, night crow—from what Way does it come? Straight child acts, crow—what like? Enlightened maiden, Zun Lu, chick listens, crow tiger walks, acts, come, bright (refrain), slight (refrain).
translations.idiomatic: The responding dragon and night crow come on the sacred Way; sage ministers heed the call as tigers march in bright array—the refrain murmurs softly at the close.

sentences.zh: 詩則夜烏道祿何來黑洛道烏奚悟如尊爾尊盧起黃華烏伯遼為國日忠雨令吾

translations.literal: Poem then—night crow, Way's blessing—from what does it come? Dark Luo Way, crow—what enlightened like? Honored you, Zun Lu rises, yellow flower crow, Bo Liao for the state, sun loyal, rain (refrain).
translations.idiomatic: The poem tells of blessings arriving on a dark road; honored sages rise like yellow blossoms, guarding the state through loyal days and timely rain—the refrain seals the verse.

sentences.zh: 伯遼夜烏若國何來日忠雨烏奚如悟姑尊盧面道康尊錄龍永烏赫赫福胙夜音微令吾

translations.literal: Bo Liao, night crow—if the state—from what does it come? Sun loyal, rain crow—what like? Enlightened maiden, Zun Lu face, Way at peace, honored record, dragon eternal, crow illustrious, illustrious, fortune, sacrificial meat, night sound, slight (refrain).
translations.idiomatic: Bo Liao comes through the night for the realm's sake; sage virtue brings peace, the dragon endures, fortune and sacrificial blessing blaze by night—the refrain fades to a whisper.

translations.literal: Above: four stanzas, "Shang Ye Piece."
translations.idiomatic: Above: four stanzas of "Shang Ye."

translations.literal: "Late Mushroom Fields"[1]
translations.idiomatic: Late Mushroom Fields

sentences.zh: 幾令吾幾令諸韓亂髮正令吾

translations.literal: (Refrain), (refrain)—all Han, disordered hair, correct (refrain).
translations.idiomatic: The refrain rolls on as Han hosts gather, hair awry in the field—the cadence closes on a firm beat.

sentences.zh: 幾令吾諸韓從聽心令吾若裏洛何來韓微令吾

translations.literal: (Refrain)—all Han follow, listen, heart (refrain)—if within, Luo—from what comes Han? Slight (refrain).
translations.idiomatic: Han warriors follow and listen with one heart; from the inner roads they come at the refrain's call.

sentences.zh: 尊盧忌盧文盧子路子路為路雞如文盧炯烏諸胙微令吾

translations.literal: Zun Lu, Ji Lu, Wen Lu, Zi Lu—Zi Lu acts as road, cock like Wen Lu, bright crow, all sacrificial meat, slight (refrain).
translations.idiomatic: Sage ministers of Lu mark the road; bright banners rise and sacrificial feasts spread—the refrain murmurs at the end.

translations.literal: (Refrain)—all Han, perhaps the lord follows (refrain).
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps the lord himself follows where the Han hosts and the refrain lead.

sentences.zh: 幾令吾幾諸或言隨令吾黑洛何來諸韓微令吾

translations.literal: (Refrain), (refrain)—all, perhaps words follow (refrain)—dark Luo, from what comes? All Han, slight (refrain).
translations.idiomatic: Words follow the refrain on the dark road as the Han warriors gather—the cadence dies away softly.

sentences.zh: 尊盧安成隨來免路路子為吾路奚如文盧炯烏諸胙微令吾

translations.literal: Zun Lu, Ancheng follows, come, escape road—Zi Lu acts as our road—what like? Wen Lu, bright crow, all sacrificial meat, slight (refrain).
translations.idiomatic: Sage ministers of Lu and Ancheng come by the open road; bright omens and feast-offerings mark the way—the refrain closes the stanza.

translations.literal: Above: nine stanzas, "Late Mushroom Fields."
translations.idiomatic: Above: nine stanzas of "Late Mushroom Fields."

translations.literal: Among Han pieces there is "Long Journey"; this is suspected to be it.
translations.idiomatic: Han's "Long Journey" is thought to be the source piece.

translations.literal: "Ai Zhang Piece"[1]
translations.idiomatic: Ai Zhang Piece

sentences.zh: 幾令吾呼曆舍居執來隨咄武子邪令烏銜針相風其右其右

translations.literal: (Refrain)—call, calendar, dwelling, abide, grasp, come, follow, exclaim, martial child (refrain)—crow holds needle, phase wind, its right, its right.
translations.idiomatic: The refrain summons warriors from their dwellings; martial sons answer as crows bear omens on the wind—right and right again the cadence turns.

sentences.zh: 幾令吾呼群議破葫執來隨吾咄武子邪令烏今烏今狖入海相風及後

translations.literal: (Refrain)—call, host deliberates, break gourd, grasp, come, follow (refrain), exclaim, martial child (refrain)—crow now, crow now, monkey enters sea, phase wind reaches behind.
translations.idiomatic: The host deliberates at the refrain's call; martial sons march as omens cross land and sea and the wind follows after.

sentences.zh: 幾令吾呼無公赫吾執來隨吾咄武子邪令烏無公赫吾婮立諸布始布

translations.literal: (Refrain)—call, no lord blazing (refrain), grasp, come, follow (refrain), exclaim, martial child (refrain)—crow, no lord blazing (refrain), stand, all cloth, begin cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Blazing lords answer the refrain; martial sons deploy as banners rise and cloth standards unfurl at the start of the rite.

translations.literal: Above: three stanzas, "Ai Zhang Piece."
translations.idiomatic: Above: three stanzas of "Ai Zhang."

sentences.zh: 鼓吹鐃歌十五篇 何承天義熙中私造

translations.literal: Fifteen drum-and-fife nao song pieces—privately composed by He Chengtian in the Yixi era.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen nao songs by He Chengtian, composed privately in the Yixi era.

translations.literal: "Crimson Road Piece"
translations.idiomatic: Crimson Road

sentences.zh: 朱路揚和鸞，翠蓋燿金華。

translations.literal: Crimson road raised harmony bells; emerald canopy blazed with golden splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Along the crimson road harmony bells rang; an emerald canopy shone with golden light.

sentences.zh: 玄牡飾樊纓，流旌拂飛霞。

translations.literal: Dark stallions adorned with bridle tassels; streaming banners brushed flying rosy clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Dark stallions wore tasseled bridles; streaming banners brushed the rosy clouds.

sentences.zh: 雄戟闢曠塗，班劒翼高車。

translations.literal: Heroic halberds opened the broad road; ranked swords winged the high chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Heroic halberds cleared the broad road; ranked swords flanked the high chariots.

sentences.zh: 三軍且莫喧，聽我奏鐃歌。

translations.literal: Three armies, do not clamor yet—hear me perform the nao song.
translations.idiomatic: Three armies, hold your noise—listen to the nao song I will play.

sentences.zh: 清鞞驚短簫，朗鼓節鳴笳。

translations.literal: Clear drums startled short panpipes; bright drums set the beat, pipes sounding.
translations.idiomatic: Clear drums answered the short pipes; bright drums marked the beat as pipes sang out.

sentences.zh: 人心惟愷豫，茲音亮且和。

translations.literal: Human hearts only joyful and at ease; this sound bright and harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Hearts were light with joy; the music rang clear and harmonious.

sentences.zh: 輕風起紅塵，渟瀾發微波。

translations.literal: Light wind raised red dust; still waves sent forth tiny ripples.
translations.idiomatic: A light wind lifted red dust; still water broke into gentle ripples.

sentences.zh: 逸韻騰天路，穨響結城阿。

translations.literal: Flowing melody soared on Heaven's road; falling resonance bound the city's slope.
translations.idiomatic: The flowing melody soared heavenward; falling echoes gathered at the city wall.

sentences.zh: 仁聲被八表，威震振九遐。

translations.literal: Benevolent sound covered the eight directions; awe and shock quaked the nine far reaches.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolent sound spread through the eight directions; awe shook the farthest reaches.

sentences.zh: 嗟嗟介胄士，勗哉念皇家。

translations.literal: Alas, alas, armored warriors—strive thus, remember the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, you armored warriors—take heart, and keep the imperial house in mind.

translations.literal: "Thinking of the Sad Duke Piece"
translations.idiomatic: Thinking of the Sad Duke

translations.literal: Thinking of the sad duke; cherishing the ceremonial robe.
translations.idiomatic: I think of the sad duke and the ceremonial robe he left behind.

translations.literal: Why did the eastern state grieve? The duke returned west.
translations.idiomatic: Why did the eastern land mourn? Because the duke went west.

sentences.zh: 公西歸，流二叔，幼主既悟，偃禾復。

translations.literal: The duke returned west; exiled the two uncles; the young lord already enlightened—fallen grain upright again.
translations.idiomatic: The duke returned west, banished the two uncles, and the young king, once enlightened, saw the fallen grain stand upright again.

translations.literal: Fallen grain upright again; sage intent declared.
translations.idiomatic: The grain stood up once more; the sage design was fulfilled.

translations.literal: Building the capital, new city—following these people.
translations.idiomatic: He built a new capital and moved with the people.

translations.literal: Following these people; virtue alone bright.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the people, and his virtue alone shone bright.

translations.literal: Instituting ritual, creating music; raising praise-sounds.
translations.idiomatic: He established ritual and made music; praise-songs rose.

translations.literal: Raising praise-songs; bringing fine auspice.
translations.idiomatic: Praise-songs rose and brought fine auspice.

translations.literal: Crying phoenix then gathered; the myriad states at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The crying phoenix came to roost; the myriad states knew peace.

translations.literal: The myriad states at ease—still not stopping.
translations.idiomatic: The myriad states were at ease, yet he did not cease his labors.

translations.literal: Gripping his hair, spitting out his meal—descending to the host of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He would grip his hair undone and leave his meal to receive the scholars below.

translations.literal: Only our lord—continuing Yi and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord alone continued the work of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou.

translations.literal: Personally beholding the flourishing age—what more to seek?
translations.idiomatic: To see this flourishing age with my own eyes—what more could I ask?

translations.literal: "Yong Li Piece"
translations.idiomatic: Yong Li

sentences.zh: 雝士多離心，荊民懷怨情。

translations.literal: Harmonious scholars mostly had divided hearts; Jing people harbored resentful feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the gentry had turned away; the people of Jing nursed bitter grievance.

sentences.zh: 二凶不量德，構難稱其兵。

translations.literal: The two villains did not measure virtue; fabricating hardship, boasting their arms.
translations.idiomatic: The two villains misjudged their strength, raised rebellion, and vaunted their armies.

sentences.zh: 王人銜朝命，正辭糾不庭。

translations.literal: The king's envoy bore the court's command; upright words corrected those who would not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: The king's envoy carried the court's command and rebuked those who refused to come to court.

sentences.zh: 上宰宣九伐，萬里舉長旌。

translations.literal: The chief minister proclaimed the nine punishments; ten thousand li raised the long banner.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister proclaimed the nine punishments; the long banner flew ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 樓船掩江濆，駟介飛重英。

translations.literal: Tower ships covered the river's edge; four-horse teams flew with layered pennants.
translations.idiomatic: Tower ships masked the riverbank; four-horse chariots raced beneath layered pennants.

sentences.zh: 歸德戒後夫，賈勇尚先鳴。

translations.literal: Returning virtue warned the laggard; trading courage, honoring those who sounded first.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue called back the laggard; courage was traded, and the first to sound the charge was honored.

sentences.zh: 逆徒既不濟，愚智亦相傾。

translations.literal: The rebel band having failed; fool and wise alike overturned each other.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels failed; wise and foolish alike were overthrown.

sentences.zh: 霜鋒未及染，鄢郢忽已清。

translations.literal: Frost blades not yet stained with blood—Yan and Ying suddenly already cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Before frost blades could even be stained with blood, Yan and Ying were already cleared.

sentences.zh: 西川無潛鱗，北渚有奔鯨。

translations.literal: Western rivers had no hidden scales; northern islets had whales rushing.
translations.idiomatic: No fish hid in the western rivers; whales surged off the northern islets.

sentences.zh: 淩威致天府，一戰夷三城。

translations.literal: Towering awe reached the celestial storehouse; one battle leveled three cities.
translations.idiomatic: Towering awe filled the celestial storehouse; one battle brought down three cities.

sentences.zh: 江漢被美化，宇宙歌太平。

translations.literal: Yangtze and Han received beautiful transformation; the cosmos sang great peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze and Han received the king's transforming grace; the cosmos sang of great peace.

sentences.zh: 惟我東郡民，曾是深推誠。

translations.literal: Only our eastern commandery people—once deeply offered sincere devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Our people of the eastern commandery once gave their deepest loyalty.

translations.literal: "Fighting South of the Wall Piece"
translations.idiomatic: Fighting South of the Wall

translations.literal: Fighting south of the wall; spanning yellow dust.
translations.idiomatic: Battle raged south of the wall under clouds of yellow dust.

translations.literal: Crimson banners flashed like lightning; thunder drums shook.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson banners flashed like lightning; thunder drums shook the field.

translations.literal: Fierce foes savage; war horses numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Savage foes pressed hard; war horses crowded the plain.

translations.literal: Deployed across, spanning the wilds—like massed clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Armies stretched across the wilds, massed like storm clouds.

translations.literal: Relying on the great host; answering the three numina.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting in the great host, they answered to the three numina.

translations.literal: What righteousness moved—the warriors forgot their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by righteousness, the warriors forgot their lives.

translations.literal: Long swords struck; powerful crossbows sounded.
translations.idiomatic: Long swords clashed; powerful crossbows sang.

translations.literal: Flying bolts flashed and dazzled; chaotic, rushing like stars.
translations.idiomatic: Bolts flew in a dazzling blur, scattering like stars in wild flight.

translations.literal: Tiger cavalry leaped; splendid pennons whirled.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger riders sprang forward; brocade pennons wheeled in the wind.

translations.literal: Crimson fire spread and rose; soaring, flying smoke.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson flame rose and spread; smoke billowed skyward.

translations.literal: Fierce heroes were cut down; high banners seized.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce champions fell; the victors pulled down the enemy's tall banners.

translations.literal: Long horns floated their calls; sound rang through clear Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Long horns sounded above the field, their voices ringing through the bright sky.

translations.literal: Leveling the band of raiders; destroying the rebel host.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel bands were crushed; the traitor host was wiped out.

translations.literal: Remaining people received blessing; singing of returning life.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors tasted grace and sang of life's return.

translations.literal: Playing triumphant music; returning to the imperial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Triumph music sounded as the army marched home to the capital.

translations.literal: Distributing ranks, presenting captives—the realm rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks were bestowed, captives presented, and the realm rejoiced.

translations.literal: "Wushan High Piece"
translations.idiomatic: "Wushan High" — title piece.

translations.literal: Wushan high; the Three Gorges steep.
translations.idiomatic: Wushan towers high; the Three Gorges stand sheer and steep.

translations.literal: Azure cliffs a thousand fathoms; deep valleys ten thousand ren.
translations.idiomatic: Azure cliffs plunge a thousand fathoms; bottomless valleys fall ten thousand ren.

translations.literal: Lofty crags crowned with numen; forests dark and dim.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred peaks wear their crown of spirit; the woods lie dark and deep.

translations.literal: Mountain birds called at night; dawn gibbons answered each other in chorus.
translations.idiomatic: Birds cry through the night; at dawn the gibbons call and answer one another.

translations.literal: Great waves surged swiftly; now carrying away, now halting.
translations.idiomatic: Great waves rush and churn, now sweeping on, now holding back.

translations.literal: Mournful, mournful—the traveling merchant guest, harboring bitter feeling.
translations.idiomatic: How mournful the merchant traveler on the road, his heart full of grief.

translations.literal: In the past, yang's ninth calamity; imperial cords faint.
translations.idiomatic: In that age of yang's ninth disaster, the imperial order had grown faint.

translations.literal: The Li house usurped the mandate; Xuan Wu blazed with numen.
translations.idiomatic: The House of Li stole Heaven's mandate, yet Huan Wen blazed with martial glory.

translations.literal: Stupid you rebel Zong; again treading chaos's mechanism.
translations.idiomatic: Foolish rebel Zong walked once more into the paths of chaos.

sentences.zh: 王旅薄伐，傳首來至京師。

translations.literal: Royal troops pressed the campaign; his head was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The king's army pressed the attack, and his head was borne to the capital.

translations.literal: In antiquity, governing a state—only virtue was prized.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients ruled their states by prizing virtue above all else.

translations.literal: Fighting by force while emptying the people—few did not topple and fall.
translations.idiomatic: To fight with all one's force and hollow out the people was, almost without exception, to fall.

translations.literal: How much more rebellion and perversity—how could it succeed?
translations.idiomatic: How much less could treason and defiance hope to succeed?

translations.literal: Take heed, you sons of Ba—do not act recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: Hear this, sons of Ba, and do not wax reckless in rebellion.

translations.literal: "Those Who Ascend the Mound Piece"
translations.idiomatic: "Those Who Ascend the Mound"

translations.literal: Those ascending the mound—each pursuing and climbing after.
translations.idiomatic: Up the burial mounds they climb, one after another.

translations.literal: Garments fine and beautiful; shaking silk and gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Dressed in fine and delicate robes, silk and gauze fluttering.

translations.literal: Leading children and infants; ascending lofty peaks.
translations.idiomatic: They lead their little children up the high ridges.

translations.literal: Looking south at the city towers—dense, lingering and turning.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing south toward the city towers, they linger in dense reflection.

translations.literal: Princes' and lords' mansions at the great road's end.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the great thoroughfare stand the mansions of princes and nobles.

translations.literal: High rafters, splendid houses; ranked vermillion galleries.
translations.idiomatic: High eaves and splendid halls, vermilion galleries in a row.

translations.literal: Overlooking the deep valley; plucking autumn orchid.
translations.idiomatic: Over the deep valley they lean and pluck autumn orchid.

translations.literal: Scholars and maidens leisurely and elegant; reflected on the lowland plain.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women stroll at ease, bright against the damp lowlands.

translations.literal: Pointing to Yingqiu; moved by Mount Niu.
translations.idiomatic: Pointing toward Yingqiu, they feel the sorrow Duke Jing knew on Mount Niu.

translations.literal: Duke Shuangjiu already gone; Duke Jing sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhuang is gone; Duke Jing can only sigh.

translations.literal: Alas—the year passes; the journey does not return.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, the year goes on, and there is no returning from this journey.

translations.literal: Ambition and spirit declined and dampened; dark temples streaked with gray.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit falters, ambition sinks; dark hair turns streaked with gray.

translations.literal: Lodging in wild weeds; tomb earth dry.
translations.idiomatic: They sleep among wild weeds; the mound's earth is already dry.

translations.literal: Looking on these mounds upon mounds—the heart turns sour.
translations.idiomatic: Looking on mound after mound, their hearts turn sore within.

translations.literal: Life must end in death—what grievance is there?
translations.idiomatic: Life ends in death—against that, what complaint can stand?

translations.literal: Take joy in today; unfold feeling and delight.
translations.idiomatic: Take what joy today allows; give full vent to feeling while you may.

translations.literal: "Bring in the Wine Piece"
translations.idiomatic: Bring in the Wine

translations.literal: Bring in the wine—celebrating the three mornings.
translations.idiomatic: Pour the wine—we celebrate through three days of rite.

translations.literal: Preparing elaborate ritual; offering fine delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: Rich ceremony is prepared; fine dishes are laid out as offerings.

translations.literal: Glory and decay exchanged; frost and mist mingled.
translations.idiomatic: Glory and decay take turns; frost and mist weave together.

translations.literal: Loosening the spring sash; summoning friends and colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: They loosen the spring sash and summon friends and colleagues.

translations.literal: Chariots matched in banners; horses aligned in bits.
translations.idiomatic: Chariots keep pace, banners matched; horses move with bits aligned.

translations.literal: Cherishing gentle restraint; rejoicing in forest moats.
translations.idiomatic: They cherish gentle restraint and take pleasure in the forest hunt.

translations.literal: Scholars lost their aim; resentful feeling toiled.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars lost their purpose; resentment wore them down.

translations.literal: Thinking of fine wine; entrusting themselves to roaming play.
translations.idiomatic: They turned to fine wine and lost themselves in wandering pleasure.

translations.literal: Men who ruined virtue—sweet to rich ale.
translations.idiomatic: Men who had ruined their virtue found rich ale sweet indeed.

translations.literal: Indulging the long night; some debauched and demonic.
translations.idiomatic: They drowned the long night in pleasure, some to the point of debauchery.

translations.literal: Raising repeated dances; harsh vulgar songs.
translations.idiomatic: Dance after dance was raised; coarse, shrill songs rang out.

translations.literal: Forms stooped and swaying; voices shouting and clamoring.
translations.idiomatic: Bodies swayed and stooped; voices shouted and clamored.

translations.literal: Heads already soaked; intent also wild.
translations.idiomatic: Heads already swimming with drink, minds already lost to folly.

translations.literal: Life and fate lost; state and house perished.
translations.idiomatic: Lives were squandered, and with them the state itself perished.

translations.literal: Alas, you later-born—moderate the drunken cup.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, you who come after—keep a measure in the cup.

translations.literal: If not wine's fault—what would be calamity?
translations.idiomatic: If wine is not to blame, then what else brings ruin?

translations.literal: "Lord's Horses Piece"
translations.idiomatic: Lord's Horses

sentences.zh: 君馬麗且閑，揚鑣騰逸姿。

translations.literal: My lord's horses beautiful and at ease; raising bridles, soaring in free grace.
translations.idiomatic: My lord's horses are beautiful and at ease, bridles lifted in effortless flight.

sentences.zh: 駿足躡流景，高步追輕飛。

translations.literal: Swift feet treading flowing light; high steps chasing light flight.
translations.idiomatic: Swift hooves tread the streaming light; long strides chase the birds on the wing.

sentences.zh: 冉冉六轡柔，奕奕金華暉。

translations.literal: Slowly, slowly the six reins soft; blazing, blazing golden flower radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Softly the six reins hang; golden splendor blazes from the caparison.

sentences.zh: 輕霄翼羽蓋，長風靡淑旂。

translations.literal: Light clouds winged the feathered canopy; long wind streamed the fair banners.
translations.idiomatic: Light clouds seem to wing the feathered canopy; long wind streams the fair banners.

sentences.zh: 願為范氏驅，雝容步中畿。

translations.literal: I wish to be Fan's driver—harmonious and at ease, walking the central domain.
translations.idiomatic: I would be Fan's charioteer, walking the capital at an easy, harmonious pace.

sentences.zh: 豈效詭遇子，馳騁趣危機。

translations.literal: How could I imitate the trickster who meets fortune—galloping toward peril's brink?
translations.idiomatic: How could I imitate the trickster who stumbles into fortune, racing toward disaster?

sentences.zh: 鉛陵策良駟，造父為之悲。

translations.literal: At Qianling he whipped fine teams—Zao Fu grieved for it.
translations.idiomatic: At Qianling he whipped his fine teams— even Zao Fu wept to see it.

sentences.zh: 不怨吳坂峻，但恨伯樂稀。

translations.literal: He did not resent Wuban's steepness—only regretted that Bole was rare.
translations.idiomatic: He did not blame Wuban's steep slope; he only mourned that men like Bole were rare.

sentences.zh: 赦彼岐山盜，實躋韓原師。

translations.literal: Pardoning those thieves of Mount Qi—truly matching the army at Hanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Pardon was granted to the thieves of Mount Qi, as once at Hanyuan the army showed mercy.

sentences.zh: 柰何漢魏主，縱情營所私。

translations.literal: Alas for Han and Wei's lords—indulging passion, scheming private ends.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for the lords of Han and Wei, who indulged their passions and schemed for private gain.

sentences.zh: 疲民甘藜藿，廄馬患盈肥。

translations.literal: Exhausted people content with coarse greens; stable horses troubled by overflowing fat.
translations.idiomatic: The exhausted people made do with coarse greens, while stable horses groaned under excess fat.

sentences.zh: 人畜貿厥養，蒼生將焉歸。

translations.literal: Men and livestock traded for their keep—where would the common people turn?
translations.idiomatic: Men and beasts were traded for fodder—where could the common people turn?

translations.literal: "Fragrant Trees Piece"
translations.idiomatic: Fragrant Trees

sentences.zh: 芳樹生北庭，豐隆正裴徊。

translations.literal: Fragrant trees grow in the northern court; Feng Long just then lingered and wandered.
translations.idiomatic: Fragrant trees grow in the northern court while the thunder god lingers above.

sentences.zh: 翠穎陵冬秀，紅葩迎春開。

translations.literal: Green tips over winter flourish; red blossoms welcome spring's opening.
translations.idiomatic: Green shoots flourish through winter; red blossoms open to greet the spring.

sentences.zh: 佳人閑幽室，惠心婉以諧。

translations.literal: The fair lady rested in a quiet chamber; gracious heart gentle and harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: The fair lady rests in her quiet chamber, her gracious heart gentle and at peace.

sentences.zh: 蘭房掩綺幌，綠草被長階。

translations.literal: Orchid room closed with gauze curtains; green grass covered the long steps.
translations.idiomatic: Silken curtains close the orchid room; green grass carpets the long steps.

sentences.zh: 日夕遊雲際，歸禽命同棲。

translations.literal: At dusk, clouds wandered the edge; returning birds destined to roost together.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk clouds drift the horizon's edge; homeward birds settle to roost as one.

sentences.zh: 皓月盈素景，涼風拂中閨。

translations.literal: Bright moon filled the pure scene; cool wind brushed the inner chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Bright moon fills the clear night; cool wind stirs the inner chamber.

sentences.zh: 哀弦理虛堂，要妙清且悽。

translations.literal: Mournful strings tuned in the empty hall—subtle, clear, and sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: Mournful strings sound in the empty hall—subtle, lucid, and full of sorrow.

sentences.zh: 嘯歌流激楚，傷此碩人懷。

translations.literal: Whistling songs flowed in fierce Chu—wounding this lofty person's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Whistling songs pour forth in fierce Chu mode, wounding the heart of this noble soul.

sentences.zh: 梁塵集丹帷，微飇揚羅袿。

translations.literal: Beam dust gathered on crimson curtains; slight breezes lifted gauze robes.
translations.idiomatic: Dust from the beams gathers on crimson curtains; a light breeze lifts her gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 豈怨嘉時莫，徒惜良願乖。

translations.literal: Did she resent the fine season's absence? Only grieved that good wishes went astray.
translations.idiomatic: She does not blame the season's passing, only that her dearest hopes have gone astray.

translations.literal: "I Have One I Think Of Piece"
translations.idiomatic: I Have One I Think Of

translations.literal: I have one I think of—thinking of men of old.
translations.idiomatic: I have one in mind—I think of the men of old.

translations.literal: Zeng and Min, the two sons—skilled in nurturing parents.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng and Min, those two sons, were masters of filial care.

translations.literal: Harmonious countenance; serving morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: With gentle faces they served their parents morning and evening.

translations.literal: Utmost sincerity, abundant and abundant—illuminating the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Sincerity heaped upon sincerity until even the spirits were moved to light.

translations.literal: Meng Ke of Zou—became minister of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius of Zou became a minister of Qi.

translations.literal: Measuring himself to receive stipend—not greedy for glory.
translations.idiomatic: He took office only as his measure allowed, and did not grasp after glory.

translations.literal: The Way not employed—alone he leaned on the pillar.
translations.idiomatic: When the Way went unused, he stood alone, leaning on the pillar.

translations.literal: Three removals already accomplished—ritual and righteousness clarified.
translations.idiomatic: After the three removals, ritual and righteousness stood clear.

translations.literal: Flying birds gathered; fierce beasts drew close.
translations.idiomatic: Birds flew in to gather; wild beasts came and drew near.

translations.literal: Merit achieved, affairs complete—then he married again.
translations.idiomatic: When his work was done and merit complete, only then did he marry again.

translations.literal: Alas for my life—meeting calamity from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for my life—I have met Heaven's harsh calamity.

translations.literal: In youth suffering bitter poison; enduring hardship.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood I tasted bitterness and knew every hardship.

translations.literal: Kind countenance cut off—meeting without cause.
translations.idiomatic: My mother's kind face is gone; there is no chance to see her again.

translations.literal: Long cherishing eternal thought—entrusted to the hill tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Long grief endures; I can only leave my thoughts at the hill tomb.

translations.literal: "Pheasant Chick Roams the Marsh Piece"
translations.idiomatic: Pheasant Chick Roams the Marsh

sentences.zh: 雉子遊原澤，初懷耿介心。

translations.literal: The pheasant chick roamed the plain marsh; at first harboring an upright, resolute heart.
translations.idiomatic: A young pheasant wandered the open marsh, at first with an upright and steadfast heart.

sentences.zh: 飲啄雖勤苦，不願棲園林，古有避世士，抗志清霄岑。

translations.literal: Drinking and pecking though toilsome—unwilling to roost in gardens and groves; in antiquity there were world-renouncing scholars who upheld their resolve on clear heaven's heights.
translations.idiomatic: Though drinking and pecking cost him toil, he would not roost in garden or grove; in antiquity, recluses held their resolve on the clear heights of heaven.

sentences.zh: 浩然寄卜肆，揮櫂通川陰。

translations.literal: With vast ease he lodged at the divination shop; waving the oar, he passed through the river's shade.
translations.idiomatic: At ease he made his home in the diviner's stall and poled his boat through the river's hidden reaches.

sentences.zh: 消搖風塵外，散髮撫鳴琴。

translations.literal: Free and wandering beyond wind and dust; loosening his hair, he stroked the sounding zither.
translations.idiomatic: Wandering free of wind and dust, hair loose, he played the ringing zither.

sentences.zh: 卿相非所眄，何況於千金。

translations.literal: Ministers and chancellors were not what he glanced at—how much less a thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: He never cast an eye toward ministers or chancellors, still less toward a thousand pieces of gold.

sentences.zh: 功名豈不美，寵辱亦相尋。

translations.literal: Fame and merit—are they not fine? Yet favor and disgrace also follow in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Fame and merit are sweet—but favor and disgrace pursue each other without rest.

sentences.zh: 冰炭結六府，憂虞纏胸襟。

translations.literal: Ice and charcoal bind the six storehouses; worry and grief coil about the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Ice and charcoal freeze the six storehouses; sorrow and care wind tight around the heart.

sentences.zh: 當世須大度，量己不克任。

translations.literal: The age demands great magnanimity; measuring oneself, one cannot bear the charge.
translations.idiomatic: The times call for a broad spirit; measured against that, one finds oneself unequal to the task.

sentences.zh: 三復泉流誡，自驚良已深。

translations.literal: Three times reviewing the spring-stream's warning—startled, I find the wound already deep.
translations.idiomatic: Three times I read the spring-stream's warning and start—already the hurt runs deep.

translations.literal: "Shang Ye Piece"
translations.idiomatic: Shang Ye

sentences.zh: 上邪下難正，眾枉不可矯。

translations.literal: What is crooked below is hard to straighten; the many warped cannot be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: When the base is crooked, the upright is hard to restore; a host of bends cannot be straightened.

sentences.zh: 音和響必清，端影緣直表。

translations.literal: When tone harmonizes, the sound must be clear; upright shadow follows the straight form.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonize the tone and the note turns clear; the true shadow follows the straight line.

sentences.zh: 大化揚仁風，齊人猶偃草。

translations.literal: Great transformation raised the wind of benevolence; even Qi's people bowed like grass.
translations.idiomatic: Great transforming virtue sent forth a benevolent wind; even the people of Qi bent like grass.

sentences.zh: 聖王既已沒，誰能弘至道。

translations.literal: The sage kings are already gone—who can spread the utmost Way?
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings have passed—who now can carry the utmost Way forward?

sentences.zh: 開春湛柔露，代終肅嚴霜。

translations.literal: Opening spring pours gentle dew; age's end brings stern frost.
translations.idiomatic: Spring opens with gentle dew; the year's end brings stern frost.

sentences.zh: 承平貴孔孟，政敝侯申商。

translations.literal: In peace, Confucius and Mencius were honored; when governance decayed, lords favored Shen and Shang.
translations.idiomatic: In settled times Confucius and Mencius were exalted; in decay the lords turned to Shen and Shang.

sentences.zh: 孝公明賞罰，六世猶克昌。

translations.literal: Duke Xiao clarified rewards and punishments; six generations still flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xiao made rewards and punishments clear; for six generations the house still prospered.

sentences.zh: 李斯肆濫刑，秦氏所以亡。

translations.literal: Li Si indulged excessive punishment; thus the Qin house perished.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si unleashed excessive punishments—and so the Qin dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 漢宣隆中興，魏祖寧三方。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han raised the mid-restoration; Cao Cao settled the three regions.
translations.idiomatic: Han Emperor Xuan restored the middle age; Cao Cao secured the three corners of the realm.

sentences.zh: 譬彼針與石，效疾故稱良。

translations.literal: Like needle and stone—they heal illness, and so are called excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Like needle and stone, they treat disease and are therefore called fine remedies.

translations.literal: "Traveling Reeds" is not ungenerous—yet how endlessly far it stretches.
translations.idiomatic: "Traveling Reeds" is not lacking in bounty—yet how endlessly it stretches away.

sentences.zh: 琴瑟時未調，改弦當更張。

translations.literal: When zither and lute are not yet tuned, change the strings—you must restring.
translations.idiomatic: When zither and lute are out of tune, one must change the strings and restring anew.

sentences.zh: 矧乃治天下，此要安可忘。

translations.literal: How much more governing all under Heaven—this essential point how could it be forgotten?
translations.idiomatic: How much more in governing all under Heaven—how could this essential truth be forgotten?

translations.literal: "Facing the High Terrace Piece"
translations.idiomatic: Facing the High Terrace

sentences.zh: 臨高臺，望天衢，飄然輕舉，陵太虛。

translations.literal: Facing the high terrace, gazing at Heaven's crossroads—floating lightly aloft, ascending the Great Void.
translations.idiomatic: From the high terrace he looked toward Heaven's roads, rising lightly into the Great Void.

translations.literal: Taking Liezi, surpassing the Emperor's homeland.
translations.idiomatic: He took Liezi and passed beyond the Emperor's domain.

translations.literal: Cloud robes, rain sashes—riding the wind in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Clothed in cloud and rain, he rode the wind in flight.

translations.literal: Solemn dragon carriage; meeting at Jade Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: With solemn dragon carriage he came to Jade Terrace.

translations.literal: Clear radiance, floating light—overflowing Penglai.
translations.idiomatic: Clear light and floating glory overflowed Penglai.

translations.literal: Crossing the western sea; bathing in the Wei River's basin.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the western sea and bathed in the Wei River's basin.

translations.literal: Standing on cloud peaks; gathering orchid in the deep.
translations.idiomatic: He stood on cloud peaks and gathered orchid in the hidden heights.

translations.literal: Galloping swift wind; roaming the Fiery Region.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped on swift wind and roamed the Fiery Region.

translations.literal: Words of longing for home; thinking of old travels.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of home with longing and remembered old journeys.

translations.literal: Tilting sky canopy; streaming lightning banners.
translations.idiomatic: The sky canopy tilted; lightning banners streamed.

translations.literal: Descending that heavenly path; sinking into deep darkness.
translations.idiomatic: He descended the heavenly road and sank into deep darkness.

translations.literal: Leaving the immortal clan; returning to the human flock.
translations.idiomatic: He left the immortal host and returned to the human throng.

translations.literal: Cherishing loyalty, embracing righteousness—serving the bright lord.
translations.idiomatic: He kept loyalty and righteousness and served the bright lord.

translations.literal: Whether blocked or smooth, following what one meets.
translations.idiomatic: Whether fortune or hardship, he followed whatever came.

translations.literal: Why distant thoughts that make the heart toil?
translations.idiomatic: Why let distant fancies weary the heart?

translations.literal: "Long Journey Piece"
translations.idiomatic: Long Journey

sentences.zh: 遠期千里客，肅駕候良辰。

translations.literal: Long journey—a guest from a thousand li; solemn carriage awaiting the fine season.
translations.idiomatic: A traveler from a thousand li came in solemn carriage, waiting for the proper season.

sentences.zh: 近命城郭友，具爾惟懿親。

translations.literal: Near command—the city friends; preparing for you, only the worthy kin.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby friends from the city gathered—all the worthy kin.

sentences.zh: 高門啟雙闈，長筵列嘉賓。

translations.literal: High gates opened double portals; long banquet arrayed with fine guests.
translations.idiomatic: High gates opened their double doors; a long feast laid out for honored guests.

sentences.zh: 中唐舞六佾，三廂羅樂人。

translations.literal: In the central hall, six rows of dancers; three wings lined with musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Six rows of dancers filled the central hall; musicians lined the three wings.

sentences.zh: 簫管激悲音，羽毛揚華文。

translations.literal: Pipes and flutes stirred mournful tones; feathers and plumes raised splendid patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Pipes and flutes raised mournful sounds; feathered dancers lifted splendid designs.

sentences.zh: 金石響高宇，絃歌動梁塵。

translations.literal: Metal and stone rang in the high hall; string songs shook dust from the beams.
translations.idiomatic: Metal and stone resounded in the lofty hall; string songs shook dust from the beams.

sentences.zh: 脩標多巧捷，九劒亦入神。

translations.literal: Elegant forms, many in clever skill; nine swords also entered the divine.
translations.idiomatic: Their elegant forms showed many clever arts; even the nine swords seemed touched by the divine.

sentences.zh: 遷善自雅調，成化由清均。

translations.literal: Moving toward goodness from refined melody; completing transformation through clear balance.
translations.idiomatic: From refined melody they moved toward goodness; through clear balance transformation was completed.

sentences.zh: 主人垂隆慶，羣士樂亡身。

translations.literal: The host bestowed lofty celebration; the host of scholars rejoiced, forgetting self.
translations.idiomatic: The host granted a grand celebration; the scholars rejoiced and forgot themselves.

sentences.zh: 願我聖明君，邇期保萬春。

translations.literal: May our sage and bright lord—near term, preserve ten thousand springs.
translations.idiomatic: May our sage and bright lord preserve ten thousand springs in the age to come.

translations.literal: "Stone Flow Piece"
translations.idiomatic: Stone Flow

translations.literal: On stone, flowing water—clear, clear its waves.
translations.idiomatic: Water flows over stone, its waves clear and bright.

translations.literal: Source in hidden peaks; forever returning to the long river.
translations.idiomatic: It rises in hidden peaks and forever returns to the long river.

translations.literal: Gazing on that which passes—the years go together.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing on what passes away, the years go with it.

translations.literal: The Master by the river—only thus does feeling increase.
translations.idiomatic: The Master by the river—only thus does feeling grow.

translations.literal: Alas for my deep grief; it toils through waking and sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for my deep grief, laboring through wake and sleep.

translations.literal: Meeting these hundred hardships—will unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: I meet a hundred hardships, and my will goes unfulfilled.

translations.literal: Years passing in a flash; long toil is what I bear.
translations.idiomatic: Years flash past; long toil is what I bear.

translations.literal: Forever speaking of perishing in the world—grieving that nothing is achieved.
translations.idiomatic: I speak forever of leaving the world, grieving that nothing is achieved.

translations.literal: Fortunate to meet opening peace; bathing in fine fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunate to meet an opening age, I bathe in fine fortune.

translations.literal: Loosening the sash, resting in sleep—what resentment then?
translations.idiomatic: Sash loosened, I rest in sleep—what resentment remains?

translations.literal: In antiquity, practicing benevolence—seeking it in oneself.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients practiced benevolence by seeking it within themselves.

translations.literal: Empty feeling, distant longing—at last only futile for oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Empty longing and distant yearning end only in futility for oneself.

sentences.zh: 《聖人制禮樂》一篇，《巾舞歌》一篇

translations.literal: "Sage Creates Ritual and Music"—one piece; "Scarf Dance Song"—one piece.
translations.idiomatic: One piece titled "The Sage Creates Ritual and Music"; one titled "Scarf Dance Song."

sentences.zh: 按《景祐廣樂記》言，字訛謬，聲辭雜書。

translations.literal: According to the Jingyou Expanded Music Record, the characters are corrupt and the sound and text are mixed in the writing.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingyou Expanded Music Record says the characters are corrupt and the words and music are jumbled together.

sentences.zh: 宋鼓吹鐃歌辭四篇，舊史言，詁不可解。

translations.literal: Four Song drum-and-fife nao song pieces—the old histories say the glosses cannot be understood.
translations.idiomatic: Four Song nao songs—the old histories say their glosses cannot be deciphered.

sentences.zh: 漢鼓吹鐃歌十八篇，按《古今樂錄》，皆聲、辭、豔相雜，不可復分。

translations.literal: Eighteen Han drum-and-fife nao song pieces—according to Old and Modern Music Records, sound, text, and flourish are all mixed and can no longer be separated.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen Han nao songs—per Old and Modern Music Records, music, text, and flourish are intermixed beyond recovery.

translations.literal: Song Shu, juan 22, textual verification.
translations.idiomatic: Textual notes on Song Shu, Music Treatise, juan 22.

sentences.zh: 樂志四《靈芝篇》：「伯瑜年七十采衣以娛親。

translations.literal: Music Treatise, "Lingzhi Piece": "Bo Yu at seventy wore colorful clothes to delight his parents."
translations.idiomatic: Music Treatise, "Lingzhi Piece": "Bo Yu at seventy wore colorful clothes to amuse his parents."

translations.literal: ○ "Bo Yu" in one edition reads "Bo Yu [alternate graph]."
translations.idiomatic: ○ One edition reads "Bo Yu" instead of "Bo Yu [alternate graph]."

translations.literal: 〈Chen Zhao〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note by Chen Zhao〉

sentences.zh: 按：《困學紀聞》引陳思王，此二語云人但知老萊子之事而不知伯瑜，顧老萊子伯瑜是否兩人亦無可考也。

translations.literal: Note: Kunxue Jiwen cites Cao Zhi on these two phrases—people only know Old Master Laizi's story and not Bo Yu; whether Laizi and Bo Yu are two men also cannot be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Kunxue Jiwen cites Cao Zhi: people know Old Master Laizi but not Bo Yu; whether they were two men cannot be verified.

translations.literal: "Mid-Winter Piece": "Bells strike the positions without remainder."
translations.idiomatic: "Mid-Winter Piece": the bells sound at every position, leaving none untouched.

translations.literal: ○ Collected Works of Cao Zhi reads "striking bells, pouring without remainder."
translations.idiomatic: ○ Cao Zhi's collected works has "striking bells, pouring without remainder."

translations.literal: "Jieshi Piece."
translations.idiomatic: Jieshi Piece

translations.literal: ○ [Editorial variant marker.]
translations.idiomatic: Editorial marker indicating a textual variant follows.

translations.literal: 〈Chen Chengcang〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note by Chen Chengcang〉

sentences.zh: 按：此曲辭即前二十一卷所載《步出夏門行》四解之一，乃魏武帝作。

translations.literal: Note: This song text is one of the four stanzas of "Stepping Out at Summer Gate" recorded in juan 21 above—it was composed by Emperor Wu of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: This lyric is one of four stanzas of "Stepping Out at Summer Gate" in juan 21—composed by Emperor Wu of Wei.

translations.literal: "Fragrant Trees Piece": "The jealous man's child sadly kills a person."
translations.idiomatic: "Fragrant Trees Piece": how the jealous man's child brings sorrow even to killing.

translations.literal: ○ Jealous: one edition reads "like."
translations.idiomatic: ○ One edition reads "like" for "jealous."

sentences.zh: 漢第五曲《翁離》今第五曲《舊邦》。

translations.literal: Han fifth piece "Weng Li" is now fifth piece "Old Homeland."
translations.idiomatic: Han's fifth piece "Weng Li" is now the fifth piece "Old Homeland."

translations.literal: ○ Weng: Jin Shu reads "Yong."
translations.idiomatic: ○ Jin Shu reads "Yong" for "Weng."

translations.literal: 〈Chen Chengcang〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Commentary by Chen Chengcang〉

sentences.zh: 按：晉鼓吹歌曲內有《時運》多一篇，題曰《古{扌雝}離行》。

translations.literal: Note: Among Jin drum-and-fife songs there is an extra "Fortune's Seasons Are Many" piece, titled "Ancient Yong Li Piece."
translations.idiomatic: Jin drum-and-fife songs include an extra "Fortune's Seasons Are Many," titled "Ancient Yong Li Piece."

translations.literal: "Yong" and "Yong" are interchangeable; written as "Weng" is an error.
translations.idiomatic: "Yong" and "Yong" are interchangeable; writing "Weng" is an error.

translations.literal: "Fortune's Auspice Piece": "Wu bandits fierce."
translations.idiomatic: "Fortune's Auspice Piece": the Wu rebels grow fierce.

translations.literal: ○ Fierce: Jin Shu reads "rebel."
translations.idiomatic: ○ Jin Shu reads "rebel" for "fierce."

translations.literal: "Xuan Receives the Mandate Piece": "Liang then died in shock; below was pacified."
translations.idiomatic: "Xuan Receives the Mandate Piece": Liang died in shock, and the realm below was pacified.

translations.literal: ○ Died: Collected Works of Fu reads "slain";
translations.idiomatic: ○ Fu's collected works reads "slain" for "died";

translations.literal: Jin Shu adds the character "peace" before "calmed."
translations.idiomatic: Jin Shu adds "peace" before "calmed."

translations.literal: "Campaigning in Liaodong Piece": "Yuan having surrendered his head."
translations.idiomatic: "Campaigning in Liaodong Piece": when Yuan surrendered his head.

translations.literal: ○ Yuan: Jin Shu reads "Gongsun"; Collected Works of Fu agrees.

translations.literal: Sheng, zhi, jin, ling and such characters form one rhyme-group; they did not know that in ancient poetry and song, all characters of the jin, geng, and qing classes are not used together with the zheng class.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, zhi, jin, and ling belong to one rhyme group; they did not know that in ancient verse, jin-, geng-, and qing-class syllables are never rhymed with zheng-class syllables.

translations.idiomatic: 〈Commentary by Chen Chengcang〉

sentences.zh: 按：《漢鼓吹鐃歌》其第十二曲曰「上邪」本無意義，「邪」字大約與「耶」同是語助辭，繆襲、傅玄盡更其名，雖依漢曲次第而辭旨各殊。

translations.literal: Note: Han drum-and-fife nao songs, the twelfth piece called "Above, Wickedness!" originally had no meaning—"xie" was roughly the same as the particle "ye"; Miao Xi and Fu Xuan entirely changed their titles; though following Han piece order, the wording and intent differ entirely.
translations.idiomatic: In the Han drum-and-fife nao songs, the twelfth piece "Shangye" originally meant nothing—xie was merely a particle like ye; Miao Xi and Fu Xuan renamed them all; though the order follows the Han pieces, the words and intent differ entirely.

sentences.zh: 第十二曲皆不用「上邪」二字，至何承天作，直以為上下之「上」、邪正之「邪」，其《雍離》一篇或作《{扌雝}離》亦無意義，何承天直以為雍州之「雍」，離合之「離」，首云「雍士多離心」，然則古人作樂府，苐各以其意為之，非有定式，古今樂錄雖言所以製曲之意，後之作者亦不盡拘若其音節，則益不可攷矣。

translations.literal: The twelfth pieces all avoid the two characters "above, wickedness"; when He Chengtian composed, he took them directly as "above" and "wicked"; his "Yong Li" piece, sometimes written "Yong Li," likewise had no meaning—He Chengtian took it directly as Yong Province's "Yong" and "parting"; the opening says "Yong's gentry mostly part in heart." Thus when ancients composed yuefu, they only followed their own intent—there was no fixed pattern; though ancient and modern music records speak of why pieces were made, later composers did not wholly bind themselves even to their melodies—still less can these be investigated.
translations.idiomatic: None of the twelfth pieces use "shang xie" as written; He Chengtian took them as "above" and "wicked." His "Yong Li"—sometimes written "Yong Li"—likewise had no fixed sense; he read it as Yong Province and "parting," opening with "Yong's men mostly part in heart." Ancients composed yuefu as each saw fit—no fixed form. Music treatises explain why pieces were made, yet later composers did not even fully follow the melodies—how much less can we recover the original?
